text.text: 1. Strong command of the source language

text: Not the textbook type. The lived, intuitive grasp of idioms, registers, rhetorical structures, implied meanings, and cultural assumptions.

text.text: 2. Strong command of the target language

text: Same as the above; listed separately to emphasize its importance.

This is often the most missing. True translation of religious material demands expertise in the field, because one unfamiliar with it cannot convey its meaning.
Someone like that is more of a bilingual tourist than a translator of Islamic texts.
The actual craft. Understanding the author’s intent, distinguishing between literal and figurative, spotting ellipses, identifying probable interpretations when the text allows for more than one.

* Don't let your style, assumptions, or shortcuts change it.
* Don’t generalize, simplify, or paraphrase in a way that loses nuance.
* Don’t allow the translation to gradually deviate from the original sense.

A translator who cannot say "I don’t know" is a liability.
Details:
* Knowing when a term, idiom, or doctrinal nuance is beyond your certainty. This requires realizing what you don't know, which is half of knowledge itself.
* Resisting the urge to "fill in gaps" with assumptions or educated guesses. This usually stems from underestimating the seriousness of the text.

These conditions are the goal; translators vary in their ability to meet them.
A clear outline, even if general, helps maintain calibration.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن بن ميهوب القداري
text: Transcription:

text.text:
وَشَيْئًا عَجِيبًا، ذَاتَ مَرَّةٍ أَتَى شَخْصٌ، أَيَّامَ الشَّيْخِ مُقْبِلٍ، أَتَى شَخْصٌ عُمُرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً، قَالَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ، يَحْفَظَ، يَتَعَلَّمَ، وَكَانَ عِنْدَهُ اهْتِمَامٌ.
وَاللَّهِ يَحْفَظُ الْحُرُوفَ، وَيَأْخُذُ كُتُبَ الْقِرَاءَةِ وَالْكِتَابَةِ، لِيَتَعَلَّمَ. مَا هِيَ إِلَّا تَقْرِيبًا، أَظُنُّ، خَمْسُ سَنَوَاتٍ أَوْ سِتٌّ، إِذَا هُوَ يَخْرُجُ مَعَنَا خَطِيبًا إِلَى صَعْدَةَ، تَعَلَّمَ، حَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ، حَفِظَ الرِّيَاضَ [رِيَاضَ الصَّالِحِينَ]، خِلَالَ سِتِّ سَنَوَاتٍ.

لَمْ يَكُنْ يَنَامُ، كَانَ سَاكِنًا فِي مِنْطَقَةِ الْمَزْرَعَةِ، وَكَانَ آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ، فِي الثُّلُثِ الْأَخِيرِ، يَأْخُذُ كُتُبَهُ وَيَخْرُجُ: "أَلِف...بَاء...تَاء"، يَعْنِي فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. يَخْرُجُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ يَحْفَظُ الْحُرُوفَ. هِمَّةٌ!

فَأَنْتَ يَا أَخِي بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ، لَا يَكُونُ عِنْدَكَ أَنَّكَ لَا تَفْهَمُ، أَنَّكَ كَذَا...
هَذِهِ كُلُّهَا وَسَاوِسُ الشَّيْطَانِ.
أَمَّا أَهْلُ الإِيمَانِ يَسْتَعِينُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَيَمْضُونَ. لَا تَقُلْ هَذَا الدَّرْسُ صَعْبٌ... هَذَا الْكِتَابُ صَعْبٌ. عُمُرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً. عُمُرُ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ سَبْعُونَ، عُمُرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً، تَمَامًا، لِحْيَتُهُ بَيْضَاءُ، مُكْتَمِلَةُ الْبَيَاضِ، لَمْ يُوجَدْ سَوَادٌ إِلَّا شَعْرُ حَاجِبِهِ فَقَطْ. وَإِلَّا فَرَأْسُهُ أَبْيَضُ وَلِحْيَتُهُ بَيْضَاءُ.

وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ.

text: المصدر: شرح الشيخ أبو عمار محمد العزازي للتحفة السنية، الدرس التاسع، الزمن: 6:29

messages.author: عبد الرحمن بن ميهوب القداري
text: Translation:

text.text:
Here’s something remarkable: once, during the time of shaykh Muqbil, a man came—he was seventy years old. He said he wanted to read, memorize, and learn, and he was genuinely interested. By Allaah, he would memorize the letters and take beginner reading and writing books to learn. It was only about, I think, five or six years before he was going out with us as a khateeb to Sa'dah. He learned, he memorized the Qur'aan, and he memorized ar-Riyaadh [Riyaadh as-Saaliheen] in six years.

He hardly slept. He was living in the farm area, and in the last part of the night, during the final third, he would take his books and go out: "Alif...baa'...taa'". He would go to the masjid and study the letters. Determination!

So you, my brother, may Allaah grant you barakah, don’t think that you "don’t understand" and so on…all of that is from the waswasah of the shaytaan.
As for people of Eemaan, they seek Allaah’s help and move forward. Don’t say, "This lesson is difficult"…"this book is difficult". He was seventy. A full seventy. His beard was white, completely white. There was no black hair except the hair of his eyebrows. His head was white and his beard was white.

And help is to be sought from Allaah alone.

Source: Lessons of at-Tuhfah as-Sunniyyah by shaykh Aboo Ammaar Muhammad al-'Uzaazy. Lesson 9, time: 6:29.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن بن ميهوب القداري
messages.text:
If someone errs, advise them, gently, clearly, and sincerely.

If you do not advise, do not add harm through judgment, gossip, or shade. Silence is better than injustice.

If you advise and they disagree, clarify your point if needed, but do not retreat into quiet condemnation. Silence after confrontation leaves both sides assuming the other is wrong.

Do not judge someone as stubborn or heedless unless you have fully discussed the matter and possess sufficient knowledge of their situation. Discussion and pushback are not obstinacy: no one is obliged to accept advice as if it were revelation.

True guidance is patience, fairness, and restraint. Wrong should be corrected with wisdom, not compounded with injustice.

messages.title: صراحة الصحابة وعدم كذبهم - الشيخ ابن عثيمين

messages.author: عبد الرحمن بن ميهوب القداري
text: Transcription:

text.text:
وَفِيهِ أَيْضًا صَراحَةُ الصَّحابَةِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمْ، حَيْثُ قالَ الرَّجُلُ: "نَعَمْ". وَلَمْ يَقُلْ: "لا، الأَمْرُ سَهْلٌ، ما أَزْعَجْتُمُونِي"، كَما نَفْعَلُهُ نَحْنُ الآنَ، لَيْسَ عِنْدَنا الصَّراحَةُ، كَصَراحَةِ هذَا الصَّحابِيِّ، لَوْ أَنَّ أَحَدًا طَرَقَ عَلَيْكَ البابَ فَخَرَجْتَ وَأَنْتَ تَأْكُلُ... تَعْلُكُ التَّمْرَةَ أَوِ اللَّحْمَ، قالَ: "عَسَى ما قَوَّمْناكَ مِنْ أَكْلِكَ...". ماذا تَقُولُ لَهُ؟ "أَبَدًا". هُوَ الآنَ يَنْظُرُ اللُّقْمَةَ بِفَمِكَ وَأَنْتَ تَقُولُ: "لا".

الَّذِي يَنْبَغِي لِلإِنْسانِ أَنْ يَكُونَ صَريحًا، يَقُولُ: "نَعَمْ أَقَمْتُمُونِي مِنْ أَكْلِي، وَلَكِنِ الأَمْرُ سَهْلٌ". أَمَّا أَنْ يَقُولَ: "لا أَبَدًا، ما قَوَّمْتُمُونِي"، كَيْفَ هذَا؟

فَالْمُهِمُّ أَنَّ الصَّحابَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمْ عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الصَّراحَةِ ما يَجْعَلُهُمْ يَقُولُونَ الشَّيءَ سَواءٌ كانَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ لَهُمْ.

وَذُكِرَ لَنا أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ مِنْ أَهْلِ هذَا البَلَدِ قَدِما فِي زَمَنٍ قَدِيمٍ، قَدِما مِنَ الحَجِّ. وَكانَ الحَجُّ فِيمَا سَبَقَ مُتْعِبًا، لِأَنَّ النَّاسَ يَحُجُّونَ عَلَى الإِبِلِ. فَجاءَ النَّاسُ يُهَنِّئُونَهُمْ بِالقُدُومِ، كَما هِيَ العادَةُ.

فَقالُوا لِأَحَدِهِما: "عَسَى ما تَكَلَّفْتَ؟". قالَ: "أَبَدًا، الحَمْدُ للهِ ما تَكَلَّفْنا".

فَقالَ لَهُ الَّذِي شارَكَهُ فِي السَّفَرِ: "لا وَاللهِ يا أَخِي إِلَّا تَكَلَّفْنا، وَلَكِنْ أَعْظَمُ لِلأَجْرِ".

فَأَيُّهُما أَصْرَحُ؟ الثَّانِي أَصْرَحُ. فَأَنْتَ قُلِ الوَاقِعَ وَاعتَذِرْ مِنْهُ، إِذا كانَ مِمَّا يُعْتَذَرُ مِنْهُ.

وَذُكِرَ لَنا أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ مِنْ أَهْلِ هذَا البَلَدِ قَدِما فِي زَمَنٍ قَدِيمٍ، قَدِما مِنَ الحَجِّ. وَكانَ الحَجُّ فِيمَا سَبَقَ مُتْعِبًا، لِأَنَّ النَّاسَ يَحُجُّونَ عَلَى الإِبِلِ. فَجاءَ النَّاسُ يُهَنِّئُونَهُمْ بِالقُدُومِ، كَما هِيَ العادَةُ.

فَقالُوا لِأَحَدِهِما: "عَسَى ما تَكَلَّفْتَ؟". قالَ: "أَبَدًا، الحَمْدُ للهِ ما تَكَلَّفْنا".

فَقالَ لَهُ الَّذِي شارَكَهُ فِي السَّفَرِ: "لا وَاللهِ يا أَخِي إِلَّا تَكَلَّفْنا، وَلَكِنْ أَعْظَمُ لِلأَجْرِ".

فَأَيُّهُما أَصْرَحُ؟ الثَّانِي أَصْرَحُ. فَأَنْتَ قُلِ الوَاقِعَ وَاعتَذِرْ مِنْهُ، إِذا كانَ مِمَّا يُعْتَذَرُ مِنْهُ.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن بن ميهوب القداري
text: Translation:

text.text:
It also shows the frankness of the companions, may Allaah be pleased with them. The man said: "Yes", rather than saying: "No, it's not a problem, you did not bother me", as we might do today. We lack frankness, frankness like that of this companion.

For example, if someone knocked on your door, and you answered while eating—chewing a date or meat—he might say: "I hope I did not interrupt your meal…". What would you say? "Not at all". He's looking at the food in your mouth and you're saying: "No".

A person should be honest and say, "Yes, you did interrupt my meal, but it’s not a problem".
But to say: "No, not at all, you didn’t interrupt me"...how can that be?

What is important is that the companions, may Allaah be pleased with them, had such frankness that they would state matters clearly, whether to their own disadvantage or advantage.

It was narrated to us that two men from this country in the past, returned from Hajj, and Hajj in earlier times was strenuous because people traveled by camels. When they arrived, people congratulated them on their return, as was customary.

They asked one of them, "hopefully, it was not too difficult?". He replied: "Not at all, alhamdulillaah, it was not difficult".

His travel companion said: "No, wallahi my brother it was indeed difficult, but the reward is greater".

Which of the two is more frank? The second one.
You should state reality, and apologize for it, if it is something that merits an apology.

text:
Allah permitted grape juice and all wholesome drinks, and He forbade intoxicating wine.

He permitted sale and trade, and He forbade usury.

He permitted marriage, and He forbade fornication.

He permitted lawful slaughter, and He forbade carrion, blood, and pork.

He permitted earning through one’s work and effort, and He forbade theft and fraud.

He permitted making images of inanimate things, and He forbade making images of animate beings.

Whoever claims that the prohibition of image-making is too narrow, then the only narrowness is in his own knowledge and faith.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن بن ميهوب القداري
messages.text:
What is the best method to learn a language?

I believe the best method depends on the learner.
A big hint is that it won't feel forced, and you won't feel like you're trying too hard, but actually enjoying the process.

The first step is building a vocabulary, and that's best done by consuming content you're interested in, otherwise your brain won't cooperate.

A basic vocabulary is necessary so your brain could start linking words in order to move on to the next step: expressing oneself, and that could be done at first by inserting Arabic words into your native language, and gradually switching to full Arabic.

It also helps communicating a lot with Arabic speakers, those you have things in common with, in order to have natural and engaging conversations.

And of course, very important: daily practice. It's common sense, but ironically easily missed.

That's my experience with languages, and as I said, the best method varies from one to another.

May Allaah grant you ease and success in this journey.

text: Why is it a common theme nowadays that Muslims are cowards?

text.text: Why is it that those that have the most to say are those that do the least?

text: Since I’ve arrived in Yemen I’ve consistently heard of people talking bad about me and others — specifically people I know who strive to do good.

text.text: For some reason their tongue can only move in their absence.

text:
Is this sincerity? 

If someone has issues with what you do but they don’t “advise” you to your face it shows their lack of sincerity.

text.text: As the Salaf mentioned, the real advisor is the one who advises you to your face, as for doing it in front of others
this is humiliation not advice! Then how about in their absence?!

text: If you have this characteristic you should be embarrassed.

text.text: May Allāh protect us from people who listen to gossip and protect us from the gossipers.

messages.text:
Strong tone, and sharp. Very necessary.

This phenomenon is also related to frankness, which I shared a clip of ibn Uthaymeen about it.

Also advise being a requirement between brothers in Eemaan.

And as mentioned by that post, courage is a necessity, because you can't confront someone who challenges your views without it. Especially if that someone is tense and has dense arguments that require a back and forth.

The best option here is to remain silent. However often one doesn't, and instead releases that urge to speak and defend his views in a malicious way.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
text: I've written something similar to it in the past:

text.text:
Vague Critiques, Hollow Guidance, Fake Techniques, Blind Reliance

There’s a pattern I’ve noticed more than once, and it never fails to frustrate: someone throws a personal accusation your way, refuses to clarify, and leaves you in complete limbo. On the surface, it might seem like advice, a warning, or even concern—but dig a little deeper, and it’s a subtle power move.

The formula is simple: Accuse your opponent through a vague critique or claim. Refuse to clarify your claim if asked for specifics. Leave them confused, unsure how to respond, and questioning themselves.

What’s happening here isn’t accidental. The vagueness is deliberate: an attempt to assert authority without accountability, letting the other person weigh their critique over you while offering no way to engage meaningfully. The effect is immediate: frustration, withdrawal, and that sinking feeling that your effort, attempt to engage, understand, or connect, aren’t welcome.

This behavior has a name in psychology: gaslighting, and stonewalling. It’s manipulative, passive-aggressive, and exhausting. Yet it comes wrapped in a shiny wrapper of "guidance" or "concern", which makes it all the more frustrating.

This is no way to learn, and no way to build a relationship. Real growth, understanding, or collaboration cannot happen when one side holds all the cards and the other is left guessing. Genuine dialogue requires clarity, respect, and reciprocity—none of which exist in this pattern.

So yes, it’s frustrating. Yes, it kills your engagement. And maybe the only sane response is: step back and protect your energy from someone who’s more interested in asserting power than actually connecting, teaching, or creating something meaningful together.

text:
Abdurrahmaan al-Qaddaary.

Source:

text.text:
سلسلة الهدى والنور--الشريط 82

من شروط الأخوة في الله

 سائل : شيخنا والله نحبك كلنا في الله.

الشيخ : جزاك الله كل خير وأحسن الله إليك وجعلنا، جعل حبنا لله حباً خالصاً، مشروطاً في التناصح في دين الله، لأن كثيرا من الناس يقول للآخر أحبك في الله، ثم يدعه وشأنه، إذا رآه قد انحرف خطأً أو عمداً، لا عليك اصبر عليه وداره إلى آخره، هذا ليس من شروط الأخوة في الله، ومن شروط الأخوة في الله هو التناصح في دين الله، فإذا رأيتني قد انحرفت أو أخطأت فعليك، أن تنصحني وتوجهني، كذلك إن أنا رأيتك أن أفعل معك مثل ما تفعل معي. 

محمد ناصر الدين الألباني

text: From al-Hudaa wa an-Noor series, Tape 82

text.text: From the Conditions of Brotherhood for the Sake of Allaah

text:
Questioner: Our shaykh, by Allaah, all of us love you for the sake of Allaah..

Shaykh: May Allaah reward you with all good, and grant you His best favors, and make our love for one another sincere, rooted in mutual advising in the religion of Allaah.

Because many people say to one another: "I love you for the sake of Allaah", then leave them be. If they see them stray—whether by mistake or deliberately—they just say: Never mind, be patient with them, just go along with them, and so on...

This is not a condition of brotherhood for the sake of Allaah.
One of the conditions of brotherhood for the sake of Allaah is mutual advising in the religion of Allaah. If you see me straying or erring, you must advise and guide me. Likewise, if I see the same with you, I must treat you as you treat me.

Muhammad Naasiruddeen al-Albaany.

-----

Translated by: Abdurrahmaan bnu Meehoob al-Qaddaaree.

تشخيص الألباني للمرض الذي يفتك بالدعوة إلى الإسلام اليوم

الشيخ: كنت أظنُّ أن المشكلة في العالم الإسلامي إنما هي فقط ابتعادهم عن فهمهم لحقيقة معنى لا إله إلا الله ، ولكني مع الزمن صرتُ أتبيَّن أن هناك مشكلة أخرى في هذا العالم تُضاف إلى المشكلة الأولى الأساسية ؛ ألا وهي بعدهم عن التوحيد ، المشكلة الأخرى أنهم أكثرهم لا يتخلَّقون بأخلاق الإسلام الصحيحة إلا بقدرٍ زهيدٍ.
Al-Albaany’s Diagnosis Of The Disease That Is Ravaging The Da'wah to Islaam today

text:
The shaykh: I used to think that the problem in the Islamic world was only being far from understanding the true meaning of laa ilaaha illa Allaah. But with time I came to realize that there is another problem in this world in addition to that primary one: them being far from tawheed. The other problem is that most of them do not embody the correct manners of Islaam except to a very small degree.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
I said: Among the reasons this sickness has grown more severe: social media.
The worst of them are Facebook and similar, and the least harmful are Telegram and WhatsApp.

Whether people like that or not.

We insist that whoever advises the youth to use them under the pretext of "competing with the disbelievers" has made a mistake. 

That is because most young people are overtaken by zeal and impulsiveness, so they publish everything they come across.

Dry grass and a spark of fire.

What should we expect from that? Nothing but chaos and tribulations.

Just as it is not suitable for everyone to author books, the same applies to posting, because it requires knowledge, wisdom, and deliberation.
At the very least, those who post online should consult someone whose knowledge they trust about what they intend to publish, just as a beginning author consults someone trustworthy in knowledge about what they have authored.

I say this as advice to myself and to my brothers. Do not find the truth burdensome, and do not be deceived by what you have become accustomed to.

والإنسان يحافظ على النعمة. عندك دفاتر قد تعبت فيها، وكتب لك عليها تعاليق، ولو ضاع الكتاب تحتاج أن تشتري كتابا قد تجده وقد لا تجده. ما كل كتاب يضيع تجده! وإذا حفظته، إن شاء الله ما سيسرقه الجن ولا الإنس، إنما التسييب يجلب الضياع. نعم.

text:
قلت: وفي هذا العديد من الفوائد، منها:
    1. توجيه الناس إلى تحمل المسؤولية ونهييهم عن اتخاذ الأعذار بما غاب.
    2. نهي الناس عن الالتفات للوساوس وترك الظنون والعمل باليقين. فلو لزمك الترجيح بين كون الكتاب سرق من قبل الجن أو ضاع بسبب الإهمال، فكل عاقل سيرجح الإهمال.
     3. التمييز بين العلماء والمشعوذين في التعامل مع مثل هذه المواقف. فالعالم ينصح لك ولا يجر عليك الظنون والاحتمالات، أما المشعوذ فيستغل شكوكك ليزرع فيك سمومه ويمتص منك الأموال، وقد يخرجك من الإيمان تدرجا، خطوة خطوة إلى أن يستسيغ قلبك نفي التوحيد وأنت لا تشعر.
    4. الإنسان بطبيعته يميل إلى عدم تحمل المسؤولية، وإلى تجنب تلقي اللوم، ولكن هذا يؤدي إلى لوم غيره، وفي كثير من الأحوال قد لا تسعف الأحوال المرء، فلا يكون جليا إلا أنه هو نفسه الملام، ولهذا يعمد إلى الغيبيات، لأنه يصعب التحقق منها، وقد لا يمكن أصلا. ولعل الشيخ فطن لهذا. 

 
----------------------------

text.text:
The questioner says: "I have lost books. Do jinn steal books?"

Sheikh Yahyaa bnu Ali al-Hajoory replied: "Keep your books safe and organized. A person must preserv blessings. You have notebooks in which you worked hard, and books with your notes; if a book is lost, you would need to buy another, which you may or may not find. Not every lost book can be found! If you preserve them, inshaa'Allaah, neither jinn nor humans will steal them. Negligence is what brings loss".

text:
I said: There are many benefits in this, including: 

    1. Directing people to take responsibility and forbidding them from making excuses based on the unwitnessed.
    2. Advising people not to pay attention to waswasah or follow conjecture, but to act on certainty. If you had to decide whether a book was stolen by jinn or lost due to negligence, any sensible person would conclude it was negligence.
    3. Distinguishing between scholars and charlatans in dealing with such situations. A scholar advises you without feeding your doubts or possibilities, while a charlatan exploits your uncertainty to poison you, take your money, and may gradually lead you away from Eemaan, step by step, until your heart becomes accustomed to denying Tawheed without you realizing it.
    4. Human nature tends toward avoiding responsibility and blame, which often shifts the blame onto others. In many situations, circumstances do not assist a person, because it is clear that he himself is at fault. Hence, some resort to the unwitnessed, because it is hard—or even impossible—to verify. Perhaps the Sheikh was aware of this.

text.text:
يقول السائل: سمعت بأنه ينزل داء في ليلة من الليالي، لذلك أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتغطية القدور أو قلبها، فهل هذا يصح؟ وهل إذا نسي الإنسان وترك الإناء مفتوحا في الليل، يأكل منه أم لا؟
أفتونا مأجورين.

أجاب الشيخ العثيمين: نعم، صحيح أن في السنة ليلة ينزل فيها داء من السماء، لا يسلم منه إلا الإناء المغطى، ولهذا ينبغي أن يغطى الإناء ولو بعود.
أما قلبه، فلا أعلم لهذا أصلا، لأن المقلوب معناه ليس فيه شيء. فلا أعلم لهذا أصلا. لكن وضع شيء عليه، يقيه مما يحدث.
لكن لو نسي، فليأكل الطعام. لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ينهى عن أكل الطعام الذي لا يغطى. ولأننا لا نعلم أي ليلة هي، قد تكون هذه الليلة، وقد تكون قبلها أو بعدها.

text:
------------------------

The questioner says: I heard that a disease descends on one night of the year, so the Messenger of Allaah, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, commanded us to cover or turn over our pots.
Is this correct?
And if a person forgets and leaves a pot uncovered at night, can they still eat from it or not?
Please give us a fatwaa, and may Allaah reward you.

Sheikh Al-Uthaymeen answered: Yes, it is true that there is a night in which a disease descends from the sky, and only covered pots are safe from it.

Therefore, one should cover pots, even with a stick.

As for turning it over, I do not know of any basis for this, because that means it contains nothing. I do not know of any evidence for this. But placing something over it protects it from what may occur.

However, if one forgets, he should eat the food, because the Prophet, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, did not forbid eating food that is not covered. Also, we do not know which night it is; it may be this night, or it may be before or after it.

text.text:
أسلوب السؤال والجواب في التعليم
الشيخ : فإن أساليب العلم وطلب العلم كثيرة متعددة ، وإن منها ما جاء ذكره صراحة في كتاب الله وفي حديث رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - ؛ ألا وهو طريقة السؤال والجواب ، الله - عز وجل - يقول في صريح كتابه : (( فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون )) ، ويقول ((فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً )) ، ونبينا - صلوت الله وسلامه عليه - قد قال في قصة معروفة في السنن : ( ألا سألوا حين جهلوا ، فإنما شفاء العيِّ السؤال ) ، قال ذلك - عليه الصلاة والسلام - حينما أُصيب أحد الصحابة في سريَّةٍ غزاها مع أصحاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - أُصيب بجراحاتٍ كثيرةٍ في بدنه ، ثم في الليل احتلم ، ولما أصبح سأل من حوله ؛ هل يجدون له رخصة في ألا يغتسل ؟ - لما به من جروح - ، فأجابوه : بأنه لا بد لك من الاغتسال ، فاغتسل ، فكان فيه حتفُه وهلاكُه ، فلما بلغ خبره رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - غضب غضبًا شديدًا وقال : ( قتلوه قاتلهم الله ، ألا سألوا حين جهلوا ! فإنما شفاء العيِّ السؤال ) . شفاء العيِّ أي : الجهل ، ما هو شفاؤه ودواؤه ؟ السؤال .

وكثيرًا ما يكون طلب العلم بطريقة السؤال والإجابة عليها أنفعَ لكثير من طلاب العلم من إلقاء المحاضرات أو الدروس الفقهية ؛ لأن هذه الدروس قد يكون فيها شيء مما لا يهمُّ المستمعين لها ، بخلاف الأسئلة ؛ فإنما يواجهها كل إنسان بما يهمُّه من حياته ومن شؤون عبادته ، وعلى هذا كان ممَّا جرينا عليه منذ عشرات السنين أن نُفسح المجال لإخواننا طلاب العلم أن يوجِّهوا أسئلتهم حتى نتوجَّه للإجابة عليها بما يسَّر الله لنا إن كان عندنا علم فيها ، وإلا فكما تعلمون نصف العلم لا أدري ، وعلى هذا فليتفضَّل الأخ الموكَّل بإلقاء الأسئلة .
Teaching By Way Of Question And Answer

text:
The shaykh: The methods of learning and seeking knowledge are many and varied. Among them is one that is mentioned explicitly in the Book of Allaah and in the hadeeth of the Messenger of Allaah, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa aalihi wa sallam. It is the method of question and answer. Allaah, Exalted and Holy He is, says plainly in His Book: { So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know }, and He says: { So ask about it one who is well informed }.

Our Prophet, salawaatu-llaahi wa salaamuhu 'alayhi, said in a well-known story in the Sunan: "Why did they not ask when they were ignorant? As the cure for ignorance is to ask". He said this, alayhi as-salaatu was-salaam, when one of the Companions was injured during a military expedition that he undertook with the Companions of the Prophet, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa sallam. He suffered many wounds, then at night he had a wet dream. When morning came he asked those around him whether he had a concession to avoid ghusl because of his injuries. 

They answered him: You must perform ghusl. So he performed it and it caused his death and destruction. When the news reached the Messenger of Allaah, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, he became extremely angry and said: "They killed him, may Allaah deal with them. Why did they not ask when they were ignorant? As the cure for ignorance is to ask".
What is its remedy and medicine of ignorance? Asking.

Often knowledge sought through questions and answers is more beneficial for many students than delivering lectures or fiqh lessons, because those lessons may contain things that do not matter to the listeners. Questions are different, because each person presents what concerns him in his life and his acts of worship. Based on this, we have followed for decades the practice of allowing our brothers, the students of knowledge, to put forward their questions so that we can answer them according to what Allaah makes easy for us. If we have knowledge of the matter, we answer; otherwise, as you know, half of knowledge is saying "I do not know". So, let the brother assigned to present the questions proceed.

text.text: ما هي نصيحة الشيخ لطالب العلم المبتدئ وهل يبدأ بالقرآن أم بمعرفة السنن والبدع ومعرفة الحديث صحة وضعفا؟

السائل : يسأل بعض الناس, فيقول : ماذا ينصح الشيخ حفظه الله طالب العلم في بداية طلبه, هل يحثه على حفظ وإتقان القرآن الكريم, أم على معرفة السنن والبدع وطلب العلم الشرعي, وصحة الأحاديث وضعفها.؟ وما هو الذي كان عليه السلف الصالح رضوان الله تعالى عليهم, معرفة القرآن أم الحديث.؟ يعني في بداية طلبهم.؟

الشيخ : هذا السؤال يتكرر عن كثير من الشباب, لا يمكن إعطاء جواب موحد, أو جامد لكل الشباب, هذا السائل مثلا, أقول له إن كنت أوتيت حفظا يساعدك على أن تحفظ القرآن, فينبغي أن تحفظ القرآن, لكن من حيث معرفتنا بواقع الناس, هل كل الناس يعطون حفظا سمحا, عندهم استطاعة للحفظ بسرعة, وضبط هذا الحفظ وإبقاؤه في أذهانهم أمدا طويلا, أنا في ظني أن هذا شيء نادر, نادر جدا, فإذا كان السائل يشعر بنفسه أنه أوتي حافظة قوية, فليعنى بحفظ القرآن, ولا ينبغي أن تكون عنايته هذه مجرد حفظ, بل عليه أن يدرس القرآن على شيخ عالم مقرئ مجود, فيحضر عنده شهورا وربما سنين, حتى يتقن قراءة القرآن كما ينبغي, وفي هذه الأثناء إذا شغل نفسه بحفظ القرآن فهو يكون نور على نور, أما أن يحفظ فقط للحفظ, ثم إذا هو تلا لا يحسن تلاوة القرآن كما أنزل, فهذا الحفظ يكون وبالا عليه, فإذن حفظ القرآن الذي ننشده ونعنيه, هو أن يحفظ كما أنزله الله عز وجل, وهذا لا يكون إلا بأن يقرأ هذا الطالب, يختم على عالم مقرئ جيد.

وبهذه المناسبة سئلت في الأمس القريب سؤالا من أحدهم, يستشيرني ويستنصحني , أنه هو شغلته مهي عاجبته, وقد دعاه بعضهم للتدريس في السعودية, قلت له: تدرس ماذا ؟ قال: القرآن, قلت مستغربا ذلك, لأني ما أعرف ذلك عنه شخصيا, قلت له: أنت تقرأ القرآن جيدا.؟ قال: نعم, قلت له: يعني أنت مجاز ؟ قال: نعم قلت : من أين ؟ قال: من وزارة الأوقاف, قلت له: إجازة وزارة الأوقاف لا قيمة لها في هذا الزمان, وإذا كنت لا تصدق, تعال صلي عندنا المغرب والعشاء, واسمع القرآن المجاز من الأوقاف, أكثر أئمة المساجد لا يحسنون تلاوة القرآن.

فلذلك لا نستطيع أن نحدد طريقا لكل طالب علم, لكن أقول كلاما موجزا, إن كان لا يستطيع الحفظ, لأنه فيه ناس حافظتهم جافة, ما عندهم قدرة لا للحفظ ولا للإثبات مع الزمن, فحينئذ ينشغل بالعلم بالفقه, بالعلوم التي لا بد له منها, لتساعده على فهم ما يقرأ, قراءة عادية من كتاب الله, ومن حديث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم, فإذا ليس هناك خطة معينة توضع لكل طالب.

أحد الحضور : الغزالي في إحياء علوم الدين, يتكلم عن قضية الخوف والرجاء, فبالأخير يقول: أيهما يقدم في إعطاءه للناس الخوف أم الرجاء ؟ فيضرب مثلا ويقول: لا نستطيع أن نقدم شيئا على الآخر, إذ هما للإنسان كالماء والخبز, فمن استغنى عن الماء نقدم له خبزا, ومن استغنى عن الخبز نقدم له ماء, فهل هذا يكون تعبيرا قريبا بعض الشيء ؟

الشيخ : أي نعم.

السائل : شيخنا هنا إن بعض الإخوة يظنون أن الشيخ ناصر لا يحث الناس على حفظ القرآن, يعني بمعنى أنه لا يذكر الناس بهذا, حتى بعضهم ما فيه عنده شيء من كتبك مع أنه طالب علم, فبعض الإخوة يستغرب يقول: ليش مكتبتك ما فيها إرواء الغليل ما فيها كذا , يعني الشيخ ما يوصي بحفظ القرآن.؟

الشيخ : لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله, اللهم إني بين ... يعني هب أن الشيخ كذلك, وهو ليس كذلك, لكن هل هذا معناه يحرم حاله من علم, يعني إن كان يؤمن بهذا العلم, ما ندري ماذا, نقول: سبحان الله !, يعني أخلاق عجيبة, إذا رأينا رجلا نحويا, ما يوم وذكر حديثا يحض الناس على تلاوة القرآن, أو حديث الرسول عليه السلام, ما نستفيد من علمه بالنحو.!

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري

text.text: Al-Albaany's Advice To Beginner Knowledge Seekers

text:
Asker: Some people ask: what does the shaykh, may Allaah preserve him, advise a student of knowledge at the beginning of his path? Does he encourage him to memorize and master the Qur'aan, or to focus on learning about the Sunnah and innovations, studying the Islamic sciences, and knowing which hadeeth is sound and which is weak? What was the practice of as-Salaf as-saalih, may Allaah be pleased with them? Did they start with the Qur'aan or with the hadeeth?

The shaykh: This is a frequently asked question by many of the youth. You can't give one rigid answer for everyone. This specific questioner, for example - if Allaah has granted you a strong memory that helps you memorize the Qur'aan, then you should memorize it. But based on what we know from reality: do all people have that easy, reliable memorization? Can they memorize quickly, retain it, and keep it strong for years? In my view, that's rare, extremely rare.

So if the questioner knows he has a strong memory, then he should devote himself to memorizing the Qur'aan. But it shouldn't be just raw memorization. He must study the Qur'aan with a knowledgeable teacher who is skilled in recitation. He should remain with him for months, maybe years, until he perfects his recitation as it should be. During that time, if he is also memorizing, then that's even better. But if he only memorizes, and then when he recites he can't actually recite the Qur'aan properly as it was revealed, then that memorization becomes a burden on him. So the memorization we aim for is memorizing it as Allaah revealed it, and that only happens when the student completes it with a capable, qualified reciter.

By the way, someone asked me just recently. He wanted my advice. He wasn't happy with his job, and someone invited him to teach in Saudi. I asked him: teach what? He said: the Qur'aan. I was surprised, because I didn't know that about him. I said: you recite the Qur'aan well? He said: yes. I asked: You have an ijaazah? He said: yes. I asked: from where? He said: from the Ministry of Waqfs. I told him: an ijaazah from the Ministry of Waqfs is worthless in our time. And if you don't believe me, come pray Maghrib and 'Ishaa' with us and listen to the Qur'aan of someone with an ijaazah from the Ministry. Most imaams of masaajid can't recite the Qur'aan properly.

So we can't establish one path for every student. I'll keep it brief: if someone can't memorize - some people just don't have the capacity, neither memorization nor long-term retention - then he should focus on knowledge: fiqh, and the sciences he needs to help him understand what he reads: normal reading of the Book of Allaah, and the hadeeth of the Messenger of Allaah, salla-laahu 'alayhi wa sallam. So there is no single plan that applies to every student.

[...]

Questioner: Some brothers think the shaykh doesn't encourage people to memorize the Qur'aan, meaning he doesn't remind them of this. Some even don't have any of your books in their library, even though they are a student of knowledge. So some brothers get surprised: why is it that your library doesn't include Irwaa' al-Ghaleel, or this and that? They think the shaykh doesn't recommend memorizing the Qur'aan.

The shaykh: Laa hawla wa laa quwwata illaa bi-llaah. Suppose the shaykh actually was like that - and he isn't - but even if he were, does that mean one should deprive themselves of knowledge? If he believes in this knowledge...we don't even know what to say...Subhaanallaah. Strange manners. If we see a grammarian who never mentions a hadith about reciting the Qur'aan or the Prophet's hadeeth, does that mean we should not benefit from his expertise in grammar?

----

I said:

text.text: Everybody is a Genius. But If You Judge a Fish by Its Ability to Climb a Tree, It Will Live Its Whole Life Believing that It is Stupid.

messages.title: ابن_باز_لا_يتمذهب
text: Honorable shaykh, some people think you adhere to a specific math-hab. Would you kindly say a word on this matter?

The fatwas I issue are not based on, nor dependent on, any math-hab, neither Ahmad's nor anyone else's.
What we rely on is carefully seeking what Allaah and His Messenger said, whether that happens to be found in the math-hab of Ahmad, or the math-hab of ash-Shaafi'y, or Maalik, or Abu Haneefah, or the Thaahirys, or some of the early Salaf.
Yes.

The point is to seek what is indicated by the Book and the Sunnah. That is what we depend on. We do not depend on the math-hab of Ahmad or anyone else. We only depend on what Allaah and His Messenger said and on what the Book and the Sunnah indicate regarding rulings. Because this is what is obligatory on every student of knowledge.
Yes.

text:
I wish for a gathering with Al-Albaany, Ibn Uthaymeen, Al-Mu'allimy, Ash-Shawkaany, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, Ath-thahaby, Ibn Abd al-Haady, Ibn Hajar, An-Nawawy, Ibn Hazm, Ibn Abd al-Barr, Ibn Hanbal, Ash-Shaafi'y, Maalik, Abu Haneefah, Sufyaan ath-Thawry, Ibn al-Mubaarak, Shu'bah, Ibn Abbaas, Ibn Umar, Abu Hurayrah, Mu'aath bnu Jabal, Ali, Uthmaan, Umar, Abu Bakr...

and the Messenger of Allaah, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa sallam.

They speak about the issues in which there were different sayings, and the Messenger of Allaah, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, settles the matter between them.

Tell me, isn't this a gathering of knowledge?

Yes, it is.

text.text: Why Al-Albaany Spoke to People Like They Were His Peers

text:
Anyone who listens to al-Albaany's recorded discussions notices that he didn't talk down to people. Whether the person in front of him was a beginner or a student of knowledge, he spoke to them with a calm confidence, inviting them into the reasoning process rather than placing them at the bottom of a ladder.
 

He didn't do this because he saw no difference between levels of knowledge. He did it because he respected a person's ability to think.

His method was simple: present the evidence clearly, ask for proof in return, and move forward step by step. The conversation felt like two people cooperating to find the truth, not a teacher crushing a student under his library.
 

That style is refreshing today, especially when so many discussions feel scripted or overly formal.

Al-Albaany's approach had a certain sharpness, but it wasn't harshness. It was confidence in the strength of proof. The science carried the authority; he didn't need to.
 

This is why his tapes still feel alive. They're not lectures to passive listeners. They're dialogues that pull you in and insist you think and reason!

text_entities.text: Why Al-Albaany Spoke to People Like They Were His Peers

Anyone who listens to al-Albaany's recorded discussions notices that he didn't talk down to people. Whether the person in front of him was a beginner or a student of knowledge, he spoke to them with a calm confidence, inviting them into the reasoning process rather than placing them at the bottom of a ladder.
 

He didn't do this because he saw no difference between levels of knowledge. He did it because he respected a person's ability to think.

His method was simple: present the evidence clearly, ask for proof in return, and move forward step by step. The conversation felt like two people cooperating to find the truth, not a teacher crushing a student under his library.
 

That style is refreshing today, especially when so many discussions feel scripted or overly formal.

Al-Albaany's approach had a certain sharpness, but it wasn't harshness. It was confidence in the strength of proof. The science carried the authority; he didn't need to.
 

This is why his tapes still feel alive. They're not lectures to passive listeners. They're dialogues that pull you in and insist you think and reason!

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
text:
There's something in the tone of the early scholars that recalibrates you. Not volume. Not theatrics. Just gravity. When you hear it or read it, you feel your inner noise settle. Standards rise. Words weigh more.

That's why I keep recommending Taareekh al-Islaam by ath-Thahaby. Not as a casual read, and not as a nostalgia trip. As a reset. In times like these, most people don't need new opinions. They need their internal compass repaired.

You don't have to read all of it. Start with the first three centuries. That alone is enough to remind you what clarity sounds like, how disagreement used to breathe, how knowledge carried humility without weakness and firmness without performance.

Read it slowly. Let the tone work on you.
It won't flatter you. It will correct you.

text.text:
Shaykh [Ibn ‘Uthaymeen] said:

Bismillaahi ar-Rahmaani ar-Raheem

The author, may Allaah have mercy on him, said in his book Riyaadh as-Saaliheen:
“Chapter: The command to of salaat upon the Prophet, salla-llaahu 'alayhi wa 'alaa aalihi wa sallam”.

A command could indicate obligation, or encouragement.
That which is obligatory means that if a person does not do it, he is sinful, disobedient, and deserving of punishment.
The meaning of encouragement is that if a person does it, he receives a reward, and if he does not do it, there is no sin upon him.

Thus, the obligatory and the encouraged agree in that both carry reward when performed, but the reward of the obligatory is greater and more abundant, due to the statement of the Prophet ﷺ in the hadeeth al-qudusy, wherein Allaah, Exalted is He, said:

“Nothing My slaves seek closeness to Me by is more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon them”.

Obligations differ from the recommended in that the one who abandons an obligation is sinful, disobedient to Allaah, and deserving of punishment, whereas the one who abandons a recommended act is not sinful, but has missed out on good.

The author, may Allaah have mercy on him, mentioned the command of salaat upon the Prophet ﷺ in an unrestricted manner. So, the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed:
Is salaat upon the Prophet ﷺ obligatory once in a lifetime, or obligatory due to specific causes, or is it not obligatory at all?

The correct view is that it is obligatory due to specific causes; otherwise, the default ruling is that it is encouraged

text: Source:
I say: What supports the position held by the shaykh, may Allaah have mercy on him, is what has been authentically reported from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him:

text.text:
In at-Taareekh al-Kabeer by al-Bukhaari (1/202, verified by al-Mu‘allimy al-Yamaany):

“Ibn ‘Umar said: When the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abu Bakr entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, leaned over him, kissed his forehead, and said:
‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. You were wholesome in life and you are wholesome in death’.
And he said: ‘Whoever used to worship Muhammad, then Muhammad has died. And whoever used to worship Allah, then Allah is over the heaven, Ever-Living and does not die’”.

text:
The point of evidence: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, did not mention salaat upon the Prophet ﷺ. This is a clear proof that it is not absolutely obligatory, which is what the shaykh stated.

Also, the statement of Imam Maalik, may Allah have mercy on him. I chose to mention it from a fatwa of the Permanent Committee, since it is a trusted source for most people:

text.text:
From Fataawa al-Lajnah ad-Daa’imah – First Collection (2/490):

“It has been been authentically reported from Maalik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said:
‘Whoever introduces into the religion something that is not from it, has claimed that Muhammad betrayed the Message’.
For Allaah, Exalted is He, says:
{ Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and chosen Islaam for you as a religion }.
So whatever was not religion on that day will not be religion today”.

text: And Allah knows best.

text.text:
6. الصورة الضوئية ليست مضاهاة لخلق الله بل هي خلق الله

الجواب:
جواب هاته الشبهة موجود في الشبهة نفسها، فعبارة "هي خلق الله" تحتمل معنيين على الأقل: أولهما أن الصورة الضوئية هي الجسم نفسه، ولا يعقل هذا. الثاني أن الصورة الضوئية هي تمثيل لخلق الله كما هو، أي أن تفاصيله من صنع الله. وظننا أن هذا هو المراد.

فمستعيناً بالله أقول: صورة الشيء هي شكله، والصورة الضوئية تُظهِر شكل الشيء المُصَوَّر. هذا ما لا يمكن إنكاره. ومعلوم أن هذا الشكل الذي تظهره، منفصل عن الشيء، فهو إذن مثيل لشكله، ليس ذات الشكل، بل هو نسخة منه.

عند الربط بين هاتين النقطتين البديهيتين، نجد أن الصورة الضوئية تظهر نسخة من صنع الله. ومنه، الصورة الضوئية مثيل لخلق الله، فنستنتج أن الصورة الضوئية مضاهاة لخلق الله.
هذا مما لا مناص منه ولا تأويل له. فمن أخرج صنع المثيل المطابق تماما من معنى المضاهاة، فهذا غير صحيح، لأنه إنكار لمصطلح لغوي متفق عليه، فالمطابقة مضاهاة تامة.
A photograph is not an imitation of Allah's creation; rather, it is Allah's creation itself.

text:
:
The answer to this misconception is found within the misconception itself. 

The phrase "it is Allah's creation" carries at least two meanings: First, that the photograph is the physical object itself, which is inconceivable. Second, that the photograph is a representation of Allah's creation as it is, meaning its details are of Allah's making. We assume this is what is intended.

Seeking Allaah's help, I say: The "image" of a thing is its form, and a photograph shows the form of the object being pictured. This cannot be denied. It is known that this form shown [in the photo] is separate from the actual object; therefore, it is a likeness of its form—not the form itself, but a copy of it.
By linking these two self-evident points, we find that a photograph shows a copy of Allah’s creation. Consequently, a photograph is a likeness of Allah’s creation; thus, we conclude that photography is an imitation (mudaahaah) of Allah's creation.

This is inescapable and leaves no room for alternative interpretation. Anyone who excludes the creation of an identical likeness from the meaning of "imitation" is incorrect, as this would be a denial of an agreed-upon linguistic term; perfect correspondence is, in fact, complete imitation.

text.text: Is it permissible to say “Allah and His Messenger know best”

Student: Is it permissible to say, “Allaah and His Messenger know best”?

Al-Uthaymeen: Yes. It is permissible to say “Allaah and His Messenger know best” in legal matters (Sharee'ah rulings), but not in natural or worldly matters. For example, if someone asks, “Will it rain tomorrow?” you say, “Allaah knows best”, not “Allah and His Messenger know best”. Is this clear? … It is permissible in matters of rulings, because the Messenger knew the legal rulings. All these legal rulings of the Sharee'ah were fixed before the Messenger’s death. No ruling is renewed after him; the lawful remains lawful, the forbidden remains forbidden. So there is no new obligation or new ruling after the Messenger.

For example, is zina (adultery) forbidden? Yes: “Allaah and His Messenger know best”, because the Messenger knew it was forbidden. Do you understand?

Legal rulings did not change after his death, and the Messenger knew them. Therefore, for any legal matter, we say, “Allaah and His Messenger know best”. For natural or worldly matters, we say, “Allaah alone knows best”.

text_entities.text: Is it permissible to say “Allah and His Messenger know best”

Student: Is it permissible to say, “Allaah and His Messenger know best”?

Al-Uthaymeen: Yes. It is permissible to say “Allaah and His Messenger know best” in legal matters (Sharee'ah rulings), but not in natural or worldly matters. For example, if someone asks, “Will it rain tomorrow?” you say, “Allaah knows best”, not “Allah and His Messenger know best”. Is this clear? … It is permissible in matters of rulings, because the Messenger knew the legal rulings. All these legal rulings of the Sharee'ah were fixed before the Messenger’s death. No ruling is renewed after him; the lawful remains lawful, the forbidden remains forbidden. So there is no new obligation or new ruling after the Messenger.

For example, is zina (adultery) forbidden? Yes: “Allaah and His Messenger know best”, because the Messenger knew it was forbidden. Do you understand?

Legal rulings did not change after his death, and the Messenger knew them. Therefore, for any legal matter, we say, “Allaah and His Messenger know best”. For natural or worldly matters, we say, “Allaah alone knows best”.

text:
When despair begins to creep into your heart — do not surrender to it. Resist it as much as you can with the remembrance of Allāh. Never despair in the mercy of Allāh, for despairing in Allāh the mercy of Allāh is from the greatest of losses.

{وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَـٰفِرُونَ}

text.text: “And never give up hope of Allāh’s Mercy. Certainly no one despairs of Allāhs Mercy, except the people who disbelieve.”
“Allah is more merciful to His servants than this mother is to her child.”

text:
Even if your heart cannot feel it yet, remember this: what happens to you is not out of neglect. What Allāh gives you is given with wisdom, generosity, and kindness — even if you cannot see the full picture.

{يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ}

text.text: “Allāh intends for you ease, and He does not want to make things difficult for you.”

text:
If you feel distant and on the edge of despair, ask yourself what Allāh Himself asked mankind:

{يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ}

text.text: “O man! What has made you careless about your Lord, al-Karīm (the Most Generous)?”
“Surely, Allāhs Mercy is (ever) near unto the good-doers.”

text:
Allāh is Gentle with you. He has always been gentle with you. And He will continue to be gentle with you. Even if you cannot feel that gentleness right now, and even if life starts to feel unbearable, know that He is looking after for you. He is always looking after you.

{إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَءُوفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ}

text.text: “Indeed, Allāh is Kind with His servants.”

text:
So never feel alone.

لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ

text.text: "Don’t be sad (or afraid), surely Allāh is with us."

text_entities.text: Are You Feeling Sad? #5

When despair begins to creep into your heart — do not surrender to it. Resist it as much as you can with the remembrance of Allāh. Never despair in the mercy of Allāh, for despairing in Allāh the mercy of Allāh is from the greatest of losses.

{وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَـٰفِرُونَ}
“And never give up hope of Allāh’s Mercy. Certainly no one despairs of Allāhs Mercy, except the people who disbelieve.”
— [Yūsuf: 87]
“Allah is more merciful to His servants than this mother is to her child.”
— [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī & Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim]

Even if your heart cannot feel it yet, remember this: what happens to you is not out of neglect. What Allāh gives you is given with wisdom, generosity, and kindness — even if you cannot see the full picture.

{يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ}
“Allāh intends for you ease, and He does not want to make things difficult for you.”
— [Al-Baqarah: 185]

If you feel distant and on the edge of despair, ask yourself what Allāh Himself asked mankind:

{يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ}
“O man! What has made you careless about your Lord, al-Karīm (the Most Generous)?”
— [Al-Infiṭār: 6]
“Surely, Allāhs Mercy is (ever) near unto the good-doers.”
— [Al-ʿArāf: 56]

Allāh is Gentle with you. He has always been gentle with you. And He will continue to be gentle with you. Even if you cannot feel that gentleness right now, and even if life starts to feel unbearable, know that He is looking after for you. He is always looking after you.

{إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَءُوفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ}
“Indeed, Allāh is Kind with His servants.”
— [Ash-Shūrā: 19]

So never feel alone.

لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ
"Don’t be sad (or afraid), surely Allāh is with us."

— [At-Tawbah: 40]

~ Abul-Ḥārith Adam وفقه الله ~

messages.title: ما حكم المرأَة التي تطلب من زوجها الجماع بكثرة ؟ الشيخ العلامة الالباني…

text.text:
السائل: امرأة كثيرة الطلب من زوجها، بالنسبة للجماع. فهو يخشى على نفسه من أن يتبع هذا الامر مرض أو ضعف. فبما يواجه هذا الشيء؟

الألباني: هو طبيعي أو مريض؟

السائل: هو طبيعي. ولكن يرضى مرة، ويعطيها ظهره مرارا.

الألباني: هذه مسألة...الحقيقة...يوجه إلى الطبيب أحسن من أن يوجه لمن؟ للفقيه.

السائل: نريد شرعا.

الألباني: سيأتيك الكلام...أنا لا أستطيع أن أقول أن هذا الشخص، هل يستطيع أن يعطيها حقها، أكثر مما وصفت أنت آنفا.
وإنما الطبيب هو الذي يحكم.
فقها، أقول أنه يجب أن يحصنها. وتحصينها لا يكون إلا بإعطائها كل حقها.
لكن هو لا يستطيع، فهذا بحث ثاني.
من الذي يحكم؟ الفقيه؟ لا.
يحكم إما هو، وإما الطبيب حينما يفحصه، ويقول له هذه الخشية التي أنت تدعيها خيال ووهم.
أو يقول: لا، ما فيك هذا النشاط الجنسي، كما تفعل، أو تزيد قليلا، أو تكثر قليلا.
هذا هو النظام. نعم.

text:
قلت: هكذا الفقيه، يوكل الأمور العلمية الجامدة للمختصين فيها، ولا يتكلم فيها حتى يصدر الخبير رأيه.

ويا ليت فعل القوم هذا في مسألة التصوير الضوئي، ولكن قدر الله وما شاء فعل.

والله المستعان.

text.text:
Questioner: A woman frequently demands from her husband regarding intercourse. He fears that this may cause him illness or weakness. How should he deal with this?

Al-Albaany: Is he healthy or sick?

Questioner: He is healthy. But sometimes he complies, and often he turns his back to her.

Al-Albani: This matter… the truth is… it is better to refer him to a doctor than to whom? To a faqeeh.

Questioner: But we want a ruling according to the Shar'.

Al-Albaany: ...and I'm leading to that… I cannot say whether this person can give her her right more than what you described earlier. Rather, it is the doctor who judges.

From a faqeeh's perspective, I would say he must fulfill her rights, and fulfilling her rights can only be achieved by giving her all that she is entitled to. But if he cannot, this is another matter.

Who rules then? The faqeeh? No. The judgment comes either from the man himself, or from the doctor when he examines him and says: "This fear that you claim is an, imagination, an illusion", or he may say: "No, you don't have that much ability for sexual activity, you may remain as you are, you may increase a bit, or decrease a little".

This is how it works. Yes.

text:
I said: This is how a faqeeh delegates scientific matters to specialists, and does not speak until the expert gives his opinion.
If only people did this regarding the issue of photography.

But Allaah does whatever He wills.

والله المستعان

صحيح مسلم

 262 ( 57 )  حدثنا  أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة ، حدثنا  أبو معاوية ،  ووكيع ، عن  الأعمش  ح وحدثنا  يحيى بن يحيى ، واللفظ له، أخبرنا  أبو معاوية ، عن  الأعمش ، عن  إبراهيم ، عن  عبد الرحمن بن يزيد ، عن  سلمان  قال :  قيل له : قد علمكم نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم كل شيء حتى  الخراءة ، قال : فقال : أجل، لقد نهانا أن نستقبل القبلة لغائط أو بول، أو أن نستنجي باليمين، أو أن نستنجي بأقل من ثلاثة أحجار، أو أن نستنجي  برجيع  أو بعظم.

text:
Salmān al-Fārisī, may Allāh be pleased with him, was told: "Your Prophet has taught you everything, even defecation".

He said: "Yes. He forbade us from facing the qiblah when relieving ourselves, from cleaning oneself with the right hand, from cleaning oneself with fewer than three stones, and from cleaning oneself with dung or with a bone".

-------

I say: Don't you dare belittle anything! Even diapers!

messages.title: هل_يجوز_للرجل_أن_يقول_للمرأة_أحبك_في_الله
messages.text:
السؤال: هل يجوز للرجل أن يقول للمرأة "أحبك في الله"؟


جواب الشيخ أبي بلال الحضرمي: ننصح بترك هذا، سدا للذرائع.

لكن إذا كنت في درس أو في بعض الدروس[، وقلت]: "...ونحن نحب المرأة الفلانية في الله لما تقوم به من الدعوة، لما تقوم به من الخير، ونصرة الخير"، فما فيه مانع. [...]

أما أن تشافهها بهذا، تراسلها بهذا، فهذا فتح باب فتنة، ونسأل الله العافية والسلامة.

حتى وإن كانت المحبة كما تقول في الله، وتزعم أنها في الله، فربما تنقلب مع الأيام.
وهي تقول لك: "وأنا أحبك في الله". [يضحك الشيخ]...وبعدها فتحت شر على نفسك.

لكن من قال نحن نحب أم كذا لما تقوم به من الخير والنفاح عن الدعوة السلفية، والصدع بها، وتعليم المسلمين وإرشاد بنات المسلمين ونساء المسلمين، فهذا ما فيه أحد يتعقب عليك أو ينتقدك.

وهي تقول لك: "وأنا أحبك في الله". [يضحك الشيخ]...وبعدها فتحت شر على نفسك.

لكن من قال نحن نحب أم كذا لما تقوم به من الخير والنفاح عن الدعوة السلفية، والصدع بها، وتعليم المسلمين وإرشاد بنات المسلمين ونساء المسلمين، فهذا ما فيه أحد يتعقب عليك أو ينتقدك.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
Question: Is it permissible for a man to say to a woman, "I love you for the sake of Allāh"?

Answer of sheikh Abu Bilāl al-Ḥadhramī: It is advised to avoid this, to close off avenues for temptation.

However, if during a lesson, [you say:] "...and we love such-and-such woman for the sake of Allāh for what she does in da'wah, for what she does of good, and for supporting good", there is no problem in that.

But to express this directly to her, or correspond with her in this way, this opens the door to fitnah, and we ask Allah for safety and protection.

Even if the love is claimed to be for the sake of Allah, it may change over time.

She may tell you, "And I love you for the sake of Allah" [the Sheikh laughs]… and then you have opened a source of trouble for yourself.

However, if one says, "We love Umm so-and-so for what she does of good, for advocating the Salafiyyah, promoting it, teaching the daughters of Muslims, and guiding Muslim women", then there is no one who can reproach or criticize you for that.

messages.title: ابن باز ينكر على من يخالف السنة ويتبع أقوال المشايخ

text.text: ابن باز ينكر على من يخالف السنة ويتبع المشايخ

السائل: يقول أنه جائز [الأخذ من اللحية]، ويستدل بقول الإمام الشافعي، وأنه صحيح.

ابن باز: ينصح ينصح، ليس لأحد كلام مع السنة، الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قصوا الشوارب وفروا اللحى، خالفوا المشركين.

السائل: ا‍‍‍‍‍‍‌‌‌‌‏لشافعي يقول أنه جائز.

ابن باز: ولو، ولو، ولو، يعلم، لشافعي وغير الشافعي، ليس بحجة في مخالفة السنة، لا الشافعي ولا غيره.

السائل: يقول المشايخ ابن باز وابن عثيمين يستدلون بقول الإمام أحمد.

ابن باز: إذا قال: قال "رسول الله..." ، انتهى، لا أحمد ولا غيره. ولا الشافعي ولا غيره. يقول ابن عباس: "يوشك أن تنزل عليكم حجارة من السماء، أقول قال رسول الله، وتقولون أبو بكر وعمر". أبو بكر وعمر، أين هم وأين الشافعي وأحمد؟ أبو بكر وعمر أعظم من الشافعي وأحمد وأبي حنيفة ومالك. أنكر عليهم ابن عباس لما خالفوا السنة لقول أبي بكر وعمر.

text:
وعلى هذا المنوال نقول:

يوشك أن تقع عليكم حجارة من السماء، نقول لكم لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المصورين، وتقولون قال الشيخ فلان: "إلا التصوير الضوئي".

جوامع الكلم. نص عام. لا مخصص له، خصوصا إن كان من السفسطة كحبس الظل والمرآة.

text.text: Ibn Bāz Denounces Those Who Go Against the Sunnah and Follow the Opinions of Scholars

Questioner: He says it is permissible [to trim the beard] and cites the opinion of Imam al-Shāfi’ī, claiming it is correct.

Ibn Bāz: He should be advised, he should be advised—no one has a say against the Sunnah. The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ says: “Trim the mustaches and let the beards grow, and differ from the mushrikeen”.

Questioner: Ash-Shāfi’ī says it is permissible.

Ibn Bāz: Even if he says so, even if, even if—he should be taught. Not ash-Shāfi’ī nor anyone else, not a proof to go against the Sunnah. Neither ash-Shāfi’ī nor anyone else.

Questioner: He says scholars like Ibn Bāz and Ibn ‘Uthaymeen cite the opinion of Imām Ahmad.

Ibn Bāz: If it is said: “The Messenger of Allāh said…”, then that’s it. Not Ahmad, not anyone else, not ash-Shāfi’ī nor anyone else. Ibn ‘Abbās says: “Rocks are about to fall upon you from the sky; I say, ‘The Messenger of Allāh said…’ and you say Abu Bakr and ‘Umar”. Abu Bakr and ‘Umar—who are they compared to ash-Shāfi’ī and Ahmad? Abu Bakr and ‘Umar are greater than ash-Shāfi’ī, Ahmad, Abu Hanīfa, and Mālik. Ibn ‘Abbās denounced those when they went against the Sunnah in favor of the saying of Abu Bakr and ‘Umar.

text:
Based on that, we say: “Rocks are about to fall upon you from the sky; we say the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ cursed the image-makers”, and you say, “Sheikh So-and-So said: ‘Except photography’”.

Jawāmi’ al-Kalim (Comprehensive Statements)
A General text, not specified by anything, especially if it is sophistry like trapping-shadows or mirrors.

text: «تاريخ الإسلام - ط التوفيقية» (1/37)

text.text: «وَقَالَ يُونُسُ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ إِسْحَاقَ، حَدَّثَنِي ثَوْرُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ، عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَخْبِرْنَا عَنْ نَفْسِكَ قَالَ: "أَنَا دَعْوَةُ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَبُشْرَى عِيسَى، وَرَأَتْ أُمِّي حِينَ حَمَلَتْ بِي كَأَنَّ نُورًا خَرَجَ مِنْهَا أَضَاءَتْ لَهُ قُصُورُ بُصْرَى مِنْ أَرْضِ الشَّامِ"»

text: Tārīkh al-Islām – at-Tawfīqiyyah ed (1/37)

text.text:
Yūnus bnu Bukayr said, from Ibn Isḥāq: Thawr ibn Yazīd narrated to me, from Khālid bni Maʿdān, from some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ, that they said:
“O Messenger of Allāh ﷺ, tell us about yourself”.
He said:
“I am the duʿā’ (supplication) of my father Ibrāhīm (1), the bushra (glad tidings) of ʿĪsā (2), and when my mother first became pregnant with me, she had a dream in which a light came out from her by which the palaces of Buṣrā, in the land of ash-Shām, were illuminated”.

text:
-------

(1) { رَبَّنَا وَٱبۡعَثۡ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولٗا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ }
Our Lord! Send amongst them a Messenger of their own (and indeed Allâh answered their invocation by sending Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), who shall recite unto them Your Verses and instruct them in the Book (this Qur’ân) and Al-Hikmah (full knowledge of the Islâmic laws and jurisprudence or wisdom or Prophethood), and purify them. Verily! You are the All-Mighty, the All-Wise." [Al-Baqarah: 129]. [Hilali and Khan ]

(2) {وَإِذۡ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡكُم مُّصَدِّقٗا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرَۢا بِرَسُولٖ يَأۡتِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِي ٱسۡمُهُۥٓ أَحۡمَدُۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا سِحۡرٞ مُّبِينٞ}
And (remember) when ‘Îsâ (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary), said: "O Children of Israel! I am the Messenger of Allâh unto you, confirming the Taurât [(Torah) which came] before me, and giving glad tidings of a Messenger to come after me, whose name shall be Ahmad. But when he (Ahmad i.e. Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) came to them with clear proofs, they said: "This is plain magic." [As-Saff: 6]. [Hilali and Khan ]

-----------

Translation and comments by ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhoob al-Qaddārī.

text.text: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمۡ وَيَهۡدِيَكُمۡ سُنَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٞ (26) وَٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ أَن تَمِيلُواْ مَيۡلًا عَظِيمٗا (27) يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمۡۚ وَخُلِقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ ضَعِيفٗا (28)

text:
سورة النساء.

26 - Allâh wishes to make clear (what is lawful and what is unlawful) to you, and to show you the ways of those before you, and accept your repentance, and Allâh is All-Knower, All-Wise.

27 - Allâh wishes to accept your repentance, but those who follow their lusts, wish that you (believers) should deviate tremendously away (from the Right Path).

28 - Allâh wishes to lighten (the burden) for you; and man was created weak (cannot be patient to leave sexual intercourse with woman).

text.text:
My companion wept when he saw the path ahead of us,
and he realized: “How could we even reach Qaysar?”

I told him:
Do not weep, your eye—
we either strive for a kingdom,
or we die, and by that we are excused.

text:
I said:
Oh, I wish my people knew
what my Lord has for patience along the long path.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that results are not in their hands.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that expanding the means of spreading good can be blameworthy.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that the end does not justify the means.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that spreading knowledge is not the ultimate goal.


لا إله إلا الله
ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
والله المستعان، وعليه التكلان.

text.text:
Ayyūb as-Sakhtiyānī, Abū Bakr al-‘Anzī, their ally

(‘Alayhi) the Imām, the Ḥāfiẓ [master of ḥadīth with exceptional retention], Sayyid al-‘Ulamā’ [chief of scholars][1], Abū Bakr ibn Abī Tamīmah Kaysān al-‘Anzī, their ally, the Baṣrī, the Ādamī.

He belonged to the generation of the younger Tābi‘īn.[2]

Birth: The year Ibn ‘Abbās died, 68 AH. [3]

He met Anas ibn Mālik, though we did not find any narration from him through Anas, even though he was in the same town and met him when he was in his twenties. [4]

I read to Isḥāq ibn Abī Bakr, that Ibn Khalīl informed us, al-Labbān informed us, al-Ḥaddād informed us, Abū Nu‘aym informed us; Sulaymān ibn Aḥmad narrated to us, ‘Abdullāh ibn Aḥmad informed me, ‘Abbās al-Narsī narrated to me, Wuhayb narrated to us, al-Ja‘d Abū ‘Uthmān narrated to us:

I heard al-Ḥasan say: “Ayyūb was the chief of the youth of the people of Baṣrah”. [5]

Through the same chain until Abū Nu‘aym, Abū ‘Alī al-Ṣawwāf narrated to us, Bishr narrated to us, al-Ḥumaydī told us, saying: “Ibn ‘Uyaynah met sixty-eight Tābi‘īn, and used to say: I have not seen anyone like Ayyūb”. [6]

Ḥabīb ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, Yusr ibn Anas al-Baghdādī informed us, Abū Yūnus al-Madīnī informed us, Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad told me: I heard Mālik say: “We would enter upon Ayyūb as-Sakhtiyānī, and when we mentioned a ḥadīth of the Messenger of Allāh (ṣallā Allāhu ‘alayhi wa-sallam), he would weep until we felt mercy for him”. [7]

Abū Ḥāmid ibn Jablah informed us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ informed us, Sa‘īd ibn ‘Āmir informed us, from Salām, who said: “Ayyūb as-Sakhtiyānī would stand all night in prayer, concealing it. When it was morning, he would raise his voice as if he just got up”. [8]

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, al-Firyābī informed us, Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, Ibn Mahdī informed us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd informed us: I heard Ayyūb, when asked: “Why do you not reflect on this (meaning opinion-based rulings)?”. He said: “A donkey was asked: ‘Do you regurgitate?’ He responded: I dislike chewing falsehood”. [9]

Sulaymān informed us, ‘Alī ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz informed us, ‘Ārim informed us, Ḥammād informed us: “I have never seen a man smile to men more than Ayyūb does”. [10]

Sulaymān informed us, Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Juthū‘ī informed us, Hudbah informed us, Salām ibn Miskīn informed us: I heard Ayyūb say: “There is no worse vile person than a sinful qāri’”. [11]

text:
[al-Thahabī, Shams ad-Dīn, Siyar A‘lām al-Nubalā’, al-Risālah edition, 15-17/6]

Translated by Abdurrahmaan bnu Meehoob Al-Qaddaary

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
[1] Those aren't just flashy titles, they're accurate descriptions of his level. Al-Imaam ath-Thahaby has a rare level of objectivity, he doesn't throw around titles like they're on sale. He's very accurate and precise.

[2] Meaning he is among the three first centuries that the Prophet ﷺ testified to their righteousness.

[3] A great way to memorize information is to make a network out of them, by connecting them as if they are a puzzle. Sometimes it's obvious, and often you need creativity.

[4] This kind of information is very critical, it could help determine whether a narration is authentic or not, by checking it against these facts.

[5] Many of the salaf were prominent since their youth.

[6] You need to imagine what that statement holds. Who's saying it, and what that number looks like in real life. Incredible!

[7] How far do you think we are from that?

[8] So that's two deeds, because masking your good deeds is a good deed itself. You may consider it three, because he's also being an example for people, so that they may wake up to pray before Fajr.
Allahu Akbar. We really don't realize how great the salaf were.

[9] I actually don't understand this analogy exactly, but I can tell he's mocking those who rely on their opinions. That includes a large portion of society in this era.
والله المستعان.

[10] That's a sunnah, because the Prophet ﷺ used to smile when he meets his companions.

[11] Qāri’: For the early salaf and companions, it is someone who memorizes the Qur'aan, recites it, and applies it. However, after that, the application aspect was no longer implied, and it was merely about memorization and being known for reciting a lot.

Comments by Abdurrahmaan bnu Meehoob Al-Qaddaary

text:
Passive aggressiveness is simply annoying.
More so if you can't realize what's annoying about it.

Well, it's a symptom of fear and weakness. Those who rely on it want control without accountability, influence without risk, and punishment without exposure. But you don’t have to play their game. Noooot at all.

The key is clarity and boundaries. Surgical, calm, decisive.
Don't decode their hidden meanings or bend yourself to guess what they "really mean". "Perhaps it's not what I think".

Ask direct questions, insist on specifics. Refuse to accept vague jabs as guidance. Call out the attack out of its mask.

Protect your energy instead of getting drawn into their emotional maze.

Don't let politeness trap you. Name the behavior calmly.

"Your point is unclear. Please clarify what you mean".
"That tone doesn't work for me. Please never use it again when speaking to me".

Stay factual, neutral, and firm. 

Weakness thrives on confusion and guilt; directness disarms it.

However, sadly, ultimately, you can't change them. You may just refuse to be their playground. Set your boundaries, demand clarity, and let cowardice remain theirs alone.
: Be careful not to go over the top and slide into rudeness and aggressiveness. Directness is calm and polite, but firm. Important distinction which should be practiced with time and care.

text.text:
Narrated from Sa‘eed ibn Jubayr, he said: Umar said to Ibn ‘Abbaas: "You possess knowledge that we do not possess".

‘Āsim ibn Kulayb narrated from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbaas, who said: "Umar would invite me among the senior companions and tell me: 'Do not speak until they have spoken'.Then he would ask me, and then turn to them and say: ‘Why do you not answer me like this young boy does, whose head is not even fully developed?'"

Mu‘ammar narrated from Al-Zuhri, who said: "The Muhaajireen told Umar: 'Why don't you invite our sons, as you call Ibn ‘Abbaas?' He said: 'That boy is remarkably mature; he asks insightful questions and has a sound intellect'".

text:
[Ath-Thahaby, Shams ad-Deen, Siyar A‘laam an-Nubalaa’, vol. 3, p. 345]


I say:
* From this, it is recommended to encourage those who show genius, even if they are young, and there is no harm in mixing them with those older than them.

* It also demonstrates the obligation to seek knowledge, even from the young.
There is no harm in distinguishing a boy from his peers.

* It also shows that a senior acknowledging the merit and high rank of a junior does not diminish the senior's own status.

* Knowledge is attained through questioning, and those endowed with a sound intellect are superior.

* Composure and prudence may appear in youth, enabling them to seek knowledge, as evidenced by Umar likening Ibn ‘Abbaas to an elder, indicating the absence of youthful recklessness.

* Conversely, youthful recklessness is an obstacle to seeking knowledge.

----------

Translation and comments by ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhoob al-Qaddārī.

text.text:
Your heart will find ease—so be patient.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Patience is light". (Narrated by Muslim)

Whenever Allah tests you, He places a spark of light in your heart to guide you through. Patience is not a burden, nor a restriction; it is a guiding light that illuminates the path even in the darkest circumstances.

Your Lord is more merciful to you than you are to yourself. He knows exactly where your pain lies and measures trials according to what will elevate you, not what will overwhelm you. When your chest feels heavy, know that relief is nearer than you imagine. Through a word, a supplication, or a small event that can change the course of your life.

Do not despair along the path of patience. At its end are doors of goodness that open only for those who endure and remain steadfast. Perhaps the night in which you weep today is the very night Allah writes a victory that will make you forget every sorrow.

text:
— Abu-l-Munthir al-Hawbānī

Translation by ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhoob al-Qaddārī.

Your Lord is more merciful to you than you are to yourself. He knows exactly where your pain lies and measures trials according to what will elevate you, not what will overwhelm you. When your chest feels heavy, know that relief is nearer than you imagine. Through a word, a supplication, or a small event that can change the course of your life.

Do not despair along the path of patience. At its end are doors of goodness that open only for those who endure and remain steadfast. Perhaps the night in which you weep today is the very night Allah writes a victory that will make you forget every sorrow.

— Abu-l-Munthir al-Hawbānī

Translation by ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhoob al-Qaddārī.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري

text.text:
Hold On...Your Lord Is Generous 

 مهلًا، فربك كريم
Hold on — your Lord is Generous.

قال الله تعالى: {قُلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا} [الإسراء: 51].
Allaah, Exalted is He, said: { Say: Perhaps it will be soon } [Al-Israa': 51]

في هذه الآية تسلية للمؤمن المنتظر وفرج للأمل الكامن في صدره،
This verse is soothing for believers who wait, and a relief for the hope hidden within their chests.

فهي تذكره أن وعد الله لا يطول على من صدق،
It reminds them that the promise of Allaah is never far for those who truly believe.

وأن ما يتمناه من خير قد يكون أقرب مما يظن،
And that the good they long for may be nearer than they imagine.

ولكن الحكيم سبحانه يؤخر لحكمة
Yet the All-Wise, Holy is He, delays for a reason full of wisdom,

ويعطي في الوقت الأنسب لعبده،
and grants at the most suitable time for His slaves.

فلتبقى القلوب معلقة بربها
So let hearts remain attached to their Lord,

واثقة أن التأخير ليس نسيانًا بل إعدادًا،
trusting that delay is not neglect, but preparation.

وأن ما كتب الله كائن في أوانه،
And that what Allaah has decreed will occur in its appointed time.

فلا تيأس إذا أبطأت الأمنية،
So do not despair when your wish seems slow to come.

فربك يقول: قل عسى أن يكون قريبًا،
For your Lord has said: Say, perhaps it will be soon.

فكن على يقين أنه قريب حقًا وإن لم تره بعد.
So be certain that it truly is near, even if you have not seen it yet.

text:
أبو المنذر الحوباني
— Abu-l-Munthir al-Hawbānī

Translation by ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhoob al-Qaddārī.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري

text.text:
He will give you until you are pleased, so be reassured 

Allaah said: { And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied }

A majestic divine promise to His Prophet, overflowing with reassurance and serenity. It is a glad tidings that the divine gift to His Prophet is not limited to worldly blessings but includes the delights of the Hereafter and complete satisfaction. Scholars have said that Allaah does not truly please His Prophet except by admitting his Ummah into Paradise. Thus, this verse is among the most hopeful in the Qur’aan for the believers.

Its meaning is: Your Lord, O Muhammad, will give you such abundance of favor and honor that you will be fully satisfied with your Lord. This was realized in his life through victory and empowerment, and it will reach its fullest on the Day of Judgment when Allaah is pleased with his intercession for his Ummah.
 
It is a verse that reminds the believer that whoever pleases Allaah will be pleased by Allaah, and that satisfaction is the ultimate form of divine gift.

text:
— Abu-l-Munthir al-Hawbānī

Translation by ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhoob al-Qaddārī.

text.text: Do not say "In shā’ Allāh" in your du‘ā’

صحيح البخاري  كتاب التوحيد  | باب : في المشيئة والإرادة، وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله. 

7464  حَدَّثَنَا  مُسَدَّدٌ ، حَدَّثَنَا  عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ ، عَنْ  عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ ، عَنْ  أَنَسٍ  قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ :  " إِذَا دَعَوْتُمُ اللَّهَ فَاعْزِمُوا فِي الدُّعَاءِ، وَلَا يَقُولَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ : إِنْ شِئْتَ فَأَعْطِنِي. فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا مُسْتَكْرِهَ لَهُ ".

text:
Sahīh al-Bukhāri – Book of Tawheed | Chapter: On Will and Volition, “But you cannot will unless Allāh wills”.

[Hadīth 7464]:
Musaddad related to us, ‘Abd al-Wārith related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Azīz, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allāh, salla-llāhu ‘alayhi wa sallam, said:

text.text: "When you supplicate to Allāh, be resolute in your du‘ā’, and you must not say: ‘If You want, then give me’. For indeed, Allāh is not compelled by anyone".

text:
This text is not written as a critique of common approaches to marriage, nor as a reaction against emotion or social norms.

It exists for a simpler reason: this is the way I think, and the way I naturally assess compatibility.

I tend toward written thought, structured reasoning, and depth over spontaneity. Over time, it became clear that intellectual resonance is not optional for me. It is how I detect alignment.

I am sharing this method for those who are already inclined toward knowledge, reflection, and careful thought, and who may recognize themselves in it.

This approach is not meant to replace established criteria, nor to dismiss other paths. It simply names a reality: some people connect most meaningfully through shared intellectual temperament.

If this resonates, it may be useful.
If it does not, nothing is lost.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
text:
How do we determine compatibility between two people?

Shared hobbies and interests?

I'm someone who doesn't believe in that.

What actually determines long-term harmony is how two minds operate: how they process ideas, withstand complexity, handle disagreement, and build on structure and meaning.

Now here's where I get specific.

I want to use my actual intellectual work, including technical treatises that demand attention, patience, and seriousness.

If someone resonates with these texts, not merely understands them, but enjoys them, returns to them, feels mentally at home in them; that is a strong signal of alignment.

Writing is sculptured thinking. It embodies the mind, not just individual thoughts. It presents the full train of reasoning, arriving at its final destination; shaped as the final mental image you feel but cannot express aloud.

Does resonance with intellectually demanding material expose personal traits?

Yes, it implies several shared traits:
* comfort with depth and abstraction
* patience with structured reasoning
* respect for rigor and boundaries
* similar thresholds for seriousness and meaning

What are those? They are cognitive compatibilities. The engine behind hobbies and interests, but way more precise.

Now, an important clarification.

Intellectual resonance is not a guarantee of good manners, emotional maturity, or readiness for marriage. Knowledge alone does not equal good character, and no serious person claims otherwise.

But this method is just a filter, not a verdict.

Character, manners, and practical marital competence are assessed separately, through known and appropriate means. This initial filter simply determines whether further assessment is worth pursuing.

But what if this filter actually taps into those other areas?

How so?

Writing, especially disciplined, technical writing, inevitably reflects more than raw knowledge. It leaks temperament. It reveals adab in disagreement, patience in explanation, honesty versus posturing, and seriousness toward responsibility.

(Consider how we come to know and love our scholars: through their work)

Someone who enjoys this kind of material is already demonstrating tolerance for effort, delayed gratification, and structured thought. These are not guarantees of good marital conduct, but they are meaningful indicators. They remove certain temperaments from the pool early. That's called filtering, just another frequency channel.

Is this method unusual? Yes.
Is it permissible? Yes.
Is it aligned with sound principles? Well, I'm filtering using knowledge, and this knowledge is the deen...

There is no requirement that compatibility filters be common; only that they be honest and lawful.

If someone can sit with my thoughts, unchanged, unmarketed, unwatered, and feel drawn rather than bored or threatened, that tells me more than months of pleasant conversation ever could.

Calm. Precise. Pure. Honest. Direct. Frank.

text.text:
17. Distinguishing between image-making (tasweer) and possessing images and looking at them

Image-making is what is prohibited; as for possessing images and looking at them, then no.

The response:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ objected to ‘Aa’ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) for possessing that curtain and that cushion, and he commanded ‘Ali ibn Abi Tālib (may Allāh be pleased with him) not to leave any image without effacing it. These are two texts that are extremely explicit. Allowing looking at images and possessing them contradicts these texts and renders them ineffective. Because if you were to apply the two texts, there would remain no image for you to possess or look at.

Likewise, images are only made in order to be possessed; were it not for the possessor, the image would not exist. So how can producing an objectionable thing be haram, while possessing it is halal? This is an obvious contradiction.

Al-Haafiẓ Ibn Ḥajar did well, spoke excellently, and was precise in Fath al-Baari when he said:
«His statement: “Indeed, the makers of these images…” indicates that the angels do not enter a bayt(*) in which there are images.

The second clause is the one indicating the reason for his refusal to enter, and he only placed the first clause before it in order to emphasize the deterrence from possessing images.

Because if the threat applies to the one who makes them, then it applies to the one who uses them; for they are only made in order to be used. Thus the maker is an indirect cause, while the user is the direct agent, and therefore more deserving of the threat».

The primary faculty by which images are perceived is sight; therefore, looking at them is the most prominent form of using them.

text:
----

(*) Bayt: House, or room.

Source: Buzoogh Dhiyaa’ al-Fajr. Page 241.
Translation by the author.
