text.text:
Chapter Four: Refuting the Specious Argument of Image-Making for the Purpose of Spreading Knowledge

We have two responses to this shubha: one brief, and the other detailed.

As for the brief response:
Photography is from the major sins when it is devoid of the intention of imitation (mudhaahaat). If this is the case, how do you deem it permissible to commit it for the sake of da‘wah to Allah? And what difference is there between you and one who deems disobedience to Allah permissible in the name of da‘wah,
and between one who says, “the end justifies the means”?

This is assuming there is benefit in image-making, because there is no benefit in it at all, given that knowledge has been transmitted across centuries through speech and writing?

And if this alleged benefit is said to be reaching the common people among whom image-making has become widespread, then subhaan Allah, this is nothing but making matters worse, for anyone with common sense.

Instead of correcting the grave error of deeming a major sin lawful, we have surrendered to reality. Allahu l-Musta‘aan.

All in all: there is no justification for committing a major sin except in a case of necessity.

As for those analogizing recording lectures to ID photographs and claiming permissibility on that basis: this is false analogy, and we are astonished at one who uses it as evidence.
Its invalidity is obvious: identification photos are imposed by governments, whereas spreading knowledge is achieved without anyone compelling us to engage in image-making, and its barakah is far greater.

messages.title: ترجوا النجاة بصوت الألباني

text.text:
ترجو النجاة ولم تسلك مسالكها
إن السفينة لا تجري على اليبس

Oh you wish for salvation but haven't taken its path
Ships never sail on dry land

text:
From the poems of Abū al-‘Atāhiyah.

Al-Albaany often mentioned these two poem verses when discussing recklessly enthusiastic people.

One should hear these two verses, and reflect on his own state.
Has he taken its path?

One should hear these two verses, and reflect on his own state.
Has he taken its path?

text.text: لا تَأمَنِ المَوتَ في طَرفٍ وَلا نَفَسٍ
إِنَّ السَفينَةَ لا تَجري عَلى اليَبَسِ
أَنّى لَكَ الصَحوُ مِن سُكرٍ وَأَنتَ مَتى
تَصِحُّ مِن سَكرَةٍ تَغشاكَ في نَكَسِ

messages.title: سورة الذاريات 55-58 تجويد عبد الباسط

text.text:
وَذَكِّرۡ فَإِنَّ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ تَنفَعُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (55)
وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ (56)
مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنۡهُم مِّن رِّزۡقٖ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطۡعِمُونِ (57)
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلۡقُوَّةِ ٱلۡمَتِينُ (58)

text:
Sūrat ath-Thāriyāt

And remind (by preaching the Qur’ân, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), for verily, the reminding profits the believers (55)

And I (Allâh) created not the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me (Alone) (56)

I seek not any provision from them (i.e. provision for themselves or for My creatures) nor do I ask that they should feed Me (i.e. feed themselves or My creatures) (57)

Verily, Allâh is the All-Provider, Owner of Power, the Most Strong (58)

Tr. Muhsin Khan and Taqi-ud-Din al-Hilali

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
I say:

Perhaps one could feel a bushrā in this, those who feel their hope diminishing, fading away.
Allāh is the Provider, Possessor of Strength, the Firm.
He grants his believing slaves relief.

Your Rabb has not created you except to worship Him.
That's a promise from Allāh, that He'll take full care of the affairs of his slaves' (in truth).

Observe how the āyāt mention reminder,
then why mankind and jinn exist,
then the fact they are helpless and powerless, and that it all comes from Allāh, ‘azza w jall.

Doesn't this help you surrender to Him?
And not occupy yourself by anything other than the reason you exist?
And that it is unreasonable not to do so?

The proof of that is how Allāh tells us He doesn't want provision from us, nor to feed Him.
Meaning, being occupied by anything other than what He created you for is similar to thinking He wants provision from you, and both are nonsense that no sane person would utter.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
In an era where everyone has a voice, everyone speaks, everyone has an opinion: words lost their weight.

They became like a dead currency. Printed to death.

Speak! It's free! Endless! Just say things! Doesn't matter how it affects people...or what they convey about me! Just SPEAK!

*sigh*

Words were the strongest back in the old days of Arabs.

Where a single word could literally kill someone.

A few poem verses could defeat an army. Yes!

Where making linguistic mistakes was shameful.

Words meant things, because they were picked.

People trusted words of the enemy, let alone a friend.
If one says something, he means every bit of it.

1+1=2
Not 11 because I felt like it.

Words mean things, PICK THEM.

text.text:
الدَّغُوْلِيُّ: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بنُ زَكَرِيَّا، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بنُ النَّضْرِ بنِ مُسَاوِرٍ، قَالَ:
قَالَ أَبِي: قُلْتُ لابْنِ المُبَارَكِ: هَلْ تَتَحَفَّظُ الحَدِيْثَ؟
فَتَغَيَّرَ لَوْنُهُ، وَقَالَ: مَا تَحَفَّظْتُ حَدِيْثاً قَطُّ، إِنَّمَا آخُذُ الكِتَابَ، فَأَنظُرُ فِيْهِ، فَمَا اشْتَهَيْتُهُ، عَلِقَ بِقَلْبِي.

text:
[الذهبي، شمس الدين ,سير أعلام النبلاء ط الرسالة ,8/392]

Ibn al-Mubārak was asked, “Do you make it a point to memorize hadīth?”.

His face changed, and he said, “I never deliberately memorize any hadīth. I just read books, and naturally memorize whatever piques my interest”.

I say: May Allāh have mercy on al-Imaam al-Albāny when he adviced knowledge seekers who don't find themselves possessing a natural gift for memorization, to instead specialize in fiqh and similar.

Don't force yourself into other people's mindsets and systems. Each one has his own strengths and weaknesses.

Do you want all of us doing the same thing?!

text:
"لا تسبوا الدهر".

"Do not curse ad-dahr".

The Arabic term ad-dahr (الدَّهر) is often rendered simply as "time", but this translation misses an important nuance.

Unlike the abstract concept of time (zaman), ad-dahr refers to the course or flow of time as experienced through events, particularly those beyond human control. It encompasses not just time itself, but the unfolding of occurrences: life, death, hardship, and fortune, that happen within it.

Therfore, I suggest not translating ad-dahr merely as "time" in contexts such as the prohibition against cursing it. A more precise rendering is:
"Do not curse the course of time".

This captures the meaning that Allāh alone directs it, and humans should not blame it for misfortune.

For example, consider the āyah:

text.text:
{وَقَالُوا مَا هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ وَمَا لَهُم بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُم إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ}
    [al-Jāthiyah: 24]

And they say: "There is nothing but our life in this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except ad-Dahr (the course of time). Yet they have no knowledge; they only conjecture".
    — Translation Hilālī & Khān

text: Tafseer as-Saʿdī explains:

text.text: Those who deny resurrection say: "Nothing destroys us except ad-Dahr". In reality, it is nothing but the habits and flow of night and day; people die and others live. Death and life are decreed by Allah, not by ad-Dahr. Thus, cursing ad-Dahr is inappropriate because it attributes power over events to something that has none; the controller is Allah alone.

text: Also, the hadīth which states:

text.text:
"Allah, exalted is He, says: 'The son of Ādam annoys Me when he says, "O wretchedness of ad-dahr!". Let none of you say, "O wretchedness of ad-dahr!", for I am ad-dahr; I turn its night and day, and when I will, I take them both away'".
    Saḥīḥ Muslim (2246), translation: al-Qaddāry

text:
Notice how ad-dahr to the events that occur to people: the flow of life and death, ease and hardship, not merely the abstract passing of time.

The Arabs use ad-dahr when referring to occurrences rather than simply measuring time.

TL;DR: In short, ad-dahr is best rendered as "the course of time" in English: it conveys both time and unfolding of events, preserving the meaning that all is under Allāh's control, and humans must not blame ad-dahr itself for misfortune.

And Allah knows best.

text.text:
These hadīths concern the etiquette of relieving oneself.

In the previous hadīth, it is prohibited for two men to speak while attending to their needs: they should remain silent, for Allāh dislikes such behavior. Each should be alone, attending to his own need without speaking.

This shows that a believer should not converse with his brother at such times.

The wisdom behind this, Allāh knows best, may be that talking could prolong the act, risk exposure to impurity, distract from necessary matters, or otherwise divert attention. 

Therefore, a believer should maintain privacy: each should shield himself from the other and refrain from speaking, for Allāh dislikes that.

text: I say: this principle also applies to using a phone in the restroom and lingering there for extended periods because of it.

س (1407) ذَكَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّم لِأَشْجِّ عَبْدِ الْقَيْسِ أَنَّ فِيهِ خَصْلَتَيْنِ ي‍ُحِبُّهُمَ‍ا اللهُ، فَمَ‍ا هُمَا؟
جـ (1407) الْ‍حِلْمُ، وَالْأَنَاةُ.

Q (1407) The Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam,  told al-Ashajj ‘Abd al-Qays that he had two traits loved by Allāh. What are they?
A (1407) Forbearance and deliberateness.

text:
Source: Kanz Al-Aṭfāl (1407). Translated by Al-Qaddāry.

I said: It helps understand this more in depth if you recall that you're commanded to be patient when making du'aa, and not rush things, and not dispair, if you think your du'aa has not been answered.
Allāh is the One to decide when, not our impatience.

Now think about this Companion, do you think he was impatient when making du'aa to Allāh?

I'd say no, because of those two traits, which were so prevalent in him that Allāh let him know through the Prophet peace be upon him. Imagine receiving such news....Allāhu Akbar!

The point is, let's take this Companion as a model.

Great are the Companions.

messages.text:
[[قصة عجيبة فيها العبرة والتذكرة]]
يقول الله الرزاق سبحانه:
" وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون ما أريد منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين"
- روى الذهبي في - سير أعلام النبلاء -

أنّ حاتم الأصم وهو من كبار الصالحين، حنّ قلبه للحج في سنة من السنوات ولا يمتلك نفقة الحج ، ولايجوز سفره بل لايجب الحج دون أن يضع نفقة الأبناء دون أن يرضوا.

- فلما أقبل الموعد رأته ابنته حزينا باكيا وكان في البنت صلاح..

فقالت له : ما يبكيك ياأبتاه ؟
قال : الحج أقبل.

قالت : ومالك لاتحج ؟
فقال : النفقة.
قالت : يرزقك الله.

قال : ونفقتكم ؟
قالت : يرزقنا الله.

قال : لكن الأمر إلى أمك.
ذهبت البنت لتذكر أمها..
وفي النهاية قالت له الأم والأبناء : اذهب إلى الحج وسيرزقنا الله.

فترك لهم نفقة 3 أيام، وذهب هو إلى الحج وليس معه مايكفيه من المال،فكان يمشي خلف القافلة ،

وفي أول الطريق لسعت عقرب رئيس القافلة، فسألوا من يقرأ عليه ويداويه،فوجدوا حاتم، فقرأ عليه فعافاه الله من ساعته.
فقال رئيس القافلة : نفقة الذهاب والإياب عليّ.

فقال:اللهم هذا تدبيرك لي فأرني تدبيرك لأهل بيتي.

مرت الأيام الثلاثة ، وانتهت النفقة عند الأبناء، وبدأ الجوع يقرص عليهم ،فبدؤوا بلوم البنت،والبنت تضحك .

فقالوا : مايضحكك والجوع يوشك أن يقضي علينا ؟!
فقالت : أبونا هذا رزاق أم آكل رزق ؟
فقالوا : آكل رزق؛وإنما الرزاق هو الله.
فقالت: ذهب آكل الرزق وبقي الرزاق،،

وهي تكلمهم وإذا بالباب يقرع،
فقالوا : من بالباب ؟
فقال الطارق : إن أمير المؤمنين يستسقيكم.
فملأت القربة بالماء،وشرب الخليفة فوجد حلاوة بالماء لم يعهدها !

فقال : من أين أتيتم بالماء ؟
قالوا:من بيت حاتم.
فقال:نادوه لأجازيه
فقالوا:هو في الحج.
فخلع أمير المؤمنين منطقه-وهي حزام من القماش الفاخر المرصع بالجواهر- ، وقال:هذه لهم.
ثم قال:من كان له عليّ يد -بمعنى«من يحبني»-
فخلع كل الوزراء والتجار منطقهم لهم ،
فتكومت المناطق فاشتراها أحد التجار بمال ملأ البيت ذهباً يكفيهم حتى الموت، وأعاد المناطق إليهم .

فاشتروا الطعام وهم يضحكون فبكت البنت .

فقالت لها الأم : أمرك عجيب يا ابنتي؛كنا نبكي من الجوع وأنت تضحكين، أما وقد فرج الله علينا فمالك تبكين؟!

قالت البنت : هذا المخلوق الذي لايملك لنفسه ضرا ولا نفعا «الخليفة» نظر إلينا نظرة عطف أغنتنا إلى الموت،فكيف بمالك الملك !!

📖 سير أعلام النبلاء -(11/487).

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
text:
Ḥātim al-Aṣamm wanted to go for Ḥajj but had no money and worried about his family. His daughter urged him to trust Allāh, and his wife and children eventually agreed. He left them provisions for three days and set out with almost nothing.

On the journey, the caravan leader was stung by a scorpion. Ḥātim treated him with recitation and he recovered, so the leader paid for Ḥatim’s travel.

Meanwhile, after the family’s provisions ran out, the Caliph happened to stop by their house for water. He found it unusually delicious and, learning it was Ḥātim’s home, gave them a valuable jeweled belt. Others followed his example, and the family received enough wealth to last them.

When the food was brought and everyone laughed with relief, the daughter began to cry. When asked why, she said she was thinking about how this helpless created being had enriched them so greatly, then what about the creator?

Source: Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ (11/487)

:
If your screen and camera cooperate to display an animate object, you're committing photography of animate beings. Even if temporary (i.e a few seconds).

The claim that "no saving occurs therefore it is not ḥarām" is invalid, because it is the same as someone drawing an animate object using a brush and paint then destroying the painting...temporary!

The problem is with mere existence, no matter how short the period is.

text.text:
زار بعض أهل العلم شيخنا ـ رحمه الله ـ في بيته، وبعد أبحاث جاء ذكر «مستدرك الحاكم» وما فيه من تصحيف، فقال شيخنا: عهدي بأخينا..... منذ زمن وقد ذكر لي بأنه ينوي إخراج «المستدرك»، وأنه قد حصل له مخطوطات.

​فقال طالب العلم لشيخنا: بأنه قد جرى حديث بينه وبين الأخ.... حول «المستدرك»، وأنه أخبره أنه يخشى إخراجه بسبب النقاد الذين همهم نقد الكتب لا لفائدة علمية ولا بأسلوب علمي حتى، وإنما بسوء أدب.

​فقال شيخنا: إذا كان هذا هو السبب فهو غير محق، فعليه أن يخرجه، ولا يضره نقد الناقدين، فإن كان نقدهم صواباً استفاد، وإن كان خطأ فيكفيه أنه خطأ.

text: الإمام الألباني كما عرفته ص٦٤ - عصام موسى هادي

text.text:
A scholar visited our Sheikh—may Allah have mercy on him—at his home. After some discussions, Al-Ḥākim's Mustadrak was mentioned, along with the misspellings it contains.

Our Sheikh said: "My last contact with our brother............  was a long time ago, and he mentioned to me that he intends to publish Al-Mustadrak and that he has obtained manuscripts for it". 

​The student of knowledge then said to our Sheikh: "A conversation took place between me and brother...........  regarding Al-Mustadrak. He told me that he fears publishing it because of critics whose only concern is criticizing books, not for any scientific benefit or even in a scientific manner, but rather with bad manners". 

​Our Sheikh replied: "If this is the reason, then he is not correct. He should publish it, and the critics' criticism will not harm him; if their criticism is correct, he benefits, and if it is wrong, it is enough that it is wrong".

text:
— Al-Imām Al-Albāny As I Knew Him (page 64), by ’Iṣām Mūsā Hādī. 

Translated by Al-Qaddārī.

Al-Albānī and His Books:
I said to our shaykh: Some brothers wish to print one of your books and distribute it purely for the sake of Allāh to students of knowledge. Our Shaykh said: Any book of mine I have ownership of, if someone wants to print it and distribute it to people without seeking profit from it, then I have no objection.

text:
Al-Albānī As I Knew Him.

I said: This, then, is permission from him for us. May Allāh reward him with good, and may Allāh increase those like him.

text.text: ذكر ابن حجر (الدرر الكامنة ٥ / ٣٥١) عن شرف الدين محمد بن أحمد بن الصاحب بهاء الدين قال: "كان ابن دقيق العيد يقيم في منزلنا بمصر في غالب الأوقات، فكنا نراه في الليل إما مصليا، وإما يمشي في جوانب البيت وهو مفكر إلى طلوع الفجر، فإذا طلع الفجر صلى الصبح، ثم اضطجع إلى ضحوة"

text:
Al-Imām Fī Ma’rifati Aḥādīth Al-Aḥkām, by Ibn Daqeeq Al-’Eid. (Ed Al-Muḥaqqiq) (1 / 15)

Ibn Daqeeq Al-’Eid used to stay up all night, either praying, or walking around the house while thinking, until dawn break.
He then prays Subḥ prayer, then sleeps until forenoon. 

I say: it's good to benefit even from how scholars used to sleep, one might find a suitable method for them.

That is because they force themselves to a system that their bodies don't fit into, which causes them a great deal of tiredness and fatigue.

Al-Imām Fī Ma’rifati Aḥādīth Al-Aḥkām, by Ibn Daqeeq Al-’Eid. (Ed Al-Muḥaqqiq) (1 / 15)

Ibn Daqeeq Al-’Eid used to stay up all night, either praying, or walking around the house while thinking, until dawn break.
He then prays Subḥ prayer, then sleeps until forenoon. 

I say: it's good to benefit even from how scholars used to sleep, one might find a suitable method for them.

That is because they force themselves to a system that their bodies don't fit into, which causes them a great deal of tiredness and fatigue.

text.text:
He was raised in ease and affluence, and was endowed with exceptional intelligence, a fluid and agile mind, and a large collection of precious books. His father was among the grandees of the people of Qurṭuba and held the office of vizier under the ʿĀmirid state. Likewise, Abū Muḥammad himself served as a vizier in his youth.

He first attained mastery in literature, historical reports, and poetry, as well as in logic (al-manṭiq) and certain branches of philosophy. These disciplines left a mark on him—would that he had been spared their influence. I have personally come across a work of his in which he urges attentiveness to logic and gives it precedence over other sciences; this pained me for his sake.

For he is a leading authority in the sciences of Islām, profoundly immersed in transmitted knowledge (al-naql), unmatched, despite a certain rigidity in him and an extreme Ẓāhirī (textual literalism) tendency in subsidiary legal matters, not in foundational principles.

text:
— al-Thahabī, Shams al-Dīn, Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ, ed. ar-Risālah, 18:186

I say: this is among the examples of al-Thahabī’s justice and fairness.

Just notice how he speaks about him, a mix of love, joy, and pain.

He holds Ibn Ḥazm as a precious diamond...that sadly got chipped...but still beautiful and unique and priceless.

It takes a genius to know a genius.

I love how scholars speak to each other over centuries.

May Allāh have mercy on them both, and unite us with them in al-Jannah.

messages.text:
I loved Ibn Hazm long before I knew other scholars. I didn't even know who Al-Albany was.

Ibn Hazm taught me how to be free, how to think from the ground up, how to dissect concepts, how to destroy arguments.

How to rely on the salaf. How to take the Qur'aan and Sunnah as the absolute source of truth.

I like what they call "his rigidity", it's a unique and powerful way of thinking. Many who criticize him for it wouldn't stand a chance against him and would need to concede to his arguments. He's very persuasive, strong in debates.

One of my wishes is a debate between him and Ibn Taymiyyah...

He's human of course, made mistakes, but it's very obvious he sought the truth. We can never claim otherwise.

May Allāh have mercy on him, and grant him al-Firdaws al-A’lā.

text: We used a similar example in our book Al-Buzūgh, p. 149, where we said:

text.text:
Did you notice what I did?

I took a photo of a book, opened it in an image viewer, and then all I did was zoom the image by ten thousand percent (10,000%).

If you can, try this on your computer, because I doubt most phone apps can zoom to that extent. And if you photographed it with a higher-resolution phone, you would need an even greater zoom level.

Now, did you notice how the image taken by my phone is nothing but small colored squares?

The original image is 963 squares wide and 1280 squares tall, meaning, it contains 1,232,640 colored squares. The phone's computer arranged and colored all these squares in less than a blink of an eye. And here is the point:
this tremendous speed is what creates the illusion that photography on phones is like a mirror. It is not.

The point is that photography is merely image-making, like drawing on paper, nothing more than organizing shapes and colors. The difference lies only in the tool, the material, and the method.

Wallāhu-l-Mustaʿān.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
text:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

Many have asked about my background and the approach I follow. I am a Salafī seeker of knowledge, mostly self-taught, who consults and trusts certain scholars, mainly from Ahl as-Sunnah in Yemen.

I’m sharing the preface written by Shaykh Abū al-Yamān ʿAdnān al-Maṣqarī (ḥafiẓahu Allāh) for one of my works, but it also shows the methodology and manhaj I try to follow.

You can also see which scholars I rely on from my posts and the things I share.

May Allah guide us to benefit from knowledge sincerely for His sake.

For more about my approach:

text.text:
Preface by Shaykh Abū al-Yamān ʿAdnān ibn Ḥusayn al-Maṣqarī al-Yamānī
May Allah preserve him

الحمدُ للهِ ربِّ العالمين، أحمده سبحانه وأشكره، وأستعينه وأستغفره، وأعوذ به من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهدِه الله فلا مُضِلَّ له، ومن يُضلِل فلا هاديَ له. وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدًا عبدُه ورسولُه، صلّى الله وسلّم وبارك عليه وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين، ومن تبعهم بإحسان إلى يوم الدين.

To proceed:

The issue of image-making—particularly the depiction of animate beings—is among the matters concerning which discussion has greatly multiplied in this age, disagreement has widened, and many people have dared to contravene that which the explicit texts have clearly stated as prohibited and sternly warned against. It has reached the point that, for some, it has become one of the familiar permissibilities, to which no attention is paid with respect to the revealed texts, nor is consideration given to the objectives of the Sharīʿah in blocking the means to shirk and ghuluww (excess).

I have examined this treatise in which our esteemed brother, the researcher ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Mīhūb al-Qaddārī—may Allah grant him success, guide his steps, and bless him in what He has bestowed upon him—has clarified the causes underlying the prohibition of depicting animate beings, refined the position on this matter in accordance with the legal proofs from the Book and Sunnah, and the methodology of the righteous Salaf in understanding and dealing with them, far removed from exaggeration or undue leniency, relying upon what he has transmitted from the works of creed, the books of Sunan, and the explanations of firmly-grounded scholars.

This research is an excerpt from the book “Buzūgh Ḍiyāʾ al-Fajr al-Waḍḍāʾ ʿalā Saḥar Masʾalat al-Taṣwīr bi-l-Aḍwāʾ” by the same author, intended to bring benefit closer and to facilitate access to a sound grounding of the issue for those for whom consulting the original work is not readily possible.

I ask Allāh, Exalted is He, to grant benefit through it; to render what he has written in this work sincerely for His Noble Face; to benefit thereby its author and its reader; and to make us and you among those who follow the truth, hold fast to the Sunnah, and venerate the rites of Allāh and the limits He set.

And the last of our supplications is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May Allāh send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muḥammad, and upon his family and all of his Companions.

Written by:
Abū al-Yamān ʿAdnān ibn Ḥusayn al-Maṣqarī
at Dār al-Ḥadīth as-Salafiyyah, Shaḥūḥ
16 Jumādā The Second 1447 AH

text.text: You Let Your Women Dress Like This at Home?

text:
!

Shaykh Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Albānī رحمه الله said:

How do Muslims live in their houses these days? They live undressed exactly like women who do not know Allāh’s Dīn ﷻ. I do not know what level this nudity has reached in the houses [here] since I am new to these lands, but with us in Syria and Egypt, then say what you want, no problem, about how far people have gone in their houses with women uncovering great amounts of their bodies above and beyond what Allāh has allowed them to, which is only places of beauty.

For example, we have been afflicted by short clothes which have no sleeves – undergarments – which in old Arabic they used to call the ‘tubbān’, and which today are known as ‘shorts’ – ‘short pants’: from beneath which the thighs are apparent. So women today – the mother and daughter wear such short clothes.

Thus, the daughter will sit in front of her mother – in fact, in front of her youthful brother who is full of strength and desire, so she lifts her leg and puts it on her thigh and thus her thigh becomes exposed, uncovered and bare, based on what? Based on the fact that ‘there are no strangers around; this is her brother!’ This goes against the aforementioned āyah because Allāh only allowed uncovering the places of adornment [zīnah]. The thighs have never been one of the places of adornment [zīnah], and they almost certainly never will.

Likewise, a woman will go out in front of her brother, let alone her going out in front of her father, with her forearms uncovered – this goes against the aforementioned āyah [which states that they should]:

text.text:
وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ

“ … not reveal their [hidden] adornments (i.e., hair, body shape, underclothes) except to their husbands.”

text: So the upper arms are not zīnah, and the armpits are not zīnah, thus, all of this remains forbidden based on his clear statement ﷺ,

Even more than that goes on: a woman, a mother, will enter the bathroom – the bathroom at home – and tell her daughter to massage her back, so she will uncover her back and breasts, and this is all the upper part of the body, as we have said, and [they claim] that there is no problem in this — where has this come from? Even though the āyah is clear that our Rabb ﷻ only allowed a woman to uncover ‘the places of adornment [zīnah],’ while the chest is not a place of zīnah, and the back is not a place of zīnah.

That is why our Salaf al-Ṣāliḥ, Allāh be pleased with them, used to live in their homes under the boundaries of uncovering what Allāh ﷻ permitted for women [to uncover]. They never had this nudity that has become widespread in Muslim countries today.

So I want to remind you of this explicit meaning of the Qurʾān, and that we cultivate ourselves upon the mannerisms of the Qurʾān and we manner our women and daughters upon that, and that we do not become affected by the atmosphere surrounding us; since most of the time it only relays disbelieving European customs. Thus, we must stop at this āyah:

text.text:
وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ

“… and not reveal their [hidden] adornments (i.e., hair, body shape, underclothes) except to their husbands.”

text: Then Allāh تعالى said:
And what is meant by “women” here is only Muslim women.

text.text:
[Translation originally from here and heavily edited by Abū Hurayrah al-Birīṭānī]

Source: https://t.me/fawaid_benefits/408

messages.text:
Today I learned something new, which helped me pin-point what exactly bothered me about some people, both in real life and online. So I thought it might help you as well and give your mind some rest and ease, inshāʾa Allāh.

Apparently, there is something called "conversational narcissism". It's when a person dominates conversations and consistently redirects the focus onto themselves.

They often speak in long monologues, show little genuine interest in others, and even when they seem attentive, it's usually just to find an opening to insert themselves back into the conversation.

The most obvious sign is that they seem oblivious, they ramble excessively, sometimes at inappropriate moments, talking mostly about themselves, their desires, or plans. This leads to a disconnect: between the conversation participants and between the discussion and its original topic.

Why do they behave this way? There are many reasons. It's not always malicious; sometimes they’re simply unaware of how they come across.

The effect on others, however, is consistent: alienation, disinterest, feeling overwhelmed, and often a sense of bizarreness.

If you need to interact with such a person, the best approach is to be gentle but honest. Let them know how you feel, using plenty of "I" statements like "I feel…" to make them aware of your perspective, and that you're a human being with feelings, not an audience behind a screen.
If that doesn't work, then you need more directness, and use methods like redirecting with questions, pausing, or calmly pointing out the topic drift. Polite frankness helps a lot here.

Allāh knows best.

ʿUmar ibn Khattāb رضي الله عنه said:

“

at the one who does not seek richness through marriage, while Allāh says in His book:

﴿إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغۡنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِ﴾ 
‘

text.text: If they are poor, Allāh will enrich them from His bounty.

text:
’ 
-- [Sūrah an-Nūr, 32]

text_entities.text:
ʿUmar ibn Khattāb رضي الله عنه said:

“
I am astonished

at the one who does not seek richness through marriage, while Allāh says in His book:

﴿إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغۡنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِ﴾ 
‘
If they are poor, Allāh will enrich them from His bounty.

’ 
-- [Sūrah an-Nūr, 32]
[Al-Musannaf (5/237)]

text.text: قيل لابن سيرين: من أكل سبع رطبات على الريق سبَّحت في بطنه، فقال ابن سيرين: لئن كان هذا هكذا فينبغي للوزينج إذا أكل أن يصلي الوتر والتراويح.

Ibn Sīrīn was told: If one eats 7 dates on an empty stomach, they will do tasbīḥ [saying Subḥāna Allāh] in his stomach. 
He replied: If that is true then if one eats almond pastry they should pray Witr and Tarāwīḥ [in his stomach].

text: Bahjat al-Majālis by Ibn Abd Al-Barr. p16

text.text: قال أبو الزناد لابن شبرمة في مناظرته له: من عندنا خرج العلم. فقال ابن شبرمة: ثم لم يعد إليكم.
Abu az-Zinād told Ibn Shibrimah while debating him: Knowledge came from us. Ibn Shibrimah replied: Then it never returned to you.

text: Bahjat al-Majālis by Ibn Abd Al-Barr. p15

text.text: أنشد ابن الرِّقاع قصيدة يذكر فيه الخمر، فقال له معاوية: أما إني قد ارتبت فيك في جودة وصف الشراب، فقال: وأنا قد ارتبت بك في معرفته.

Ibn ar-Riqā’ recited a poem about wine, so Mu’āwiyah told him: You described the drink so well I'm now suspicious of you. He replied: And I'm suspicious of you because you were able to tell what I described.

text: Bahjat al-Majālis by Ibn Abd Al-Barr. p14

text.text: قالت جارية ابن السَّمَّاك له: ما أحسن كلامك إلا أنك تردده. قال: أردده حتى يفهمه من لم يكن فهمه. قالت: فإلى أن يفهمه من لم يكن فهمه يمله من فهمه.

A slave woman of Ibn as-Sammāk told him: Your speech is so excellent, however you keep repeating it. He said: I repeat it so that those who didn't understand could understand it. She said: At that point where those who didn't understand could understand it, those who understood it get bored of it.

text: Bahjat al-Majālis by Ibn Abd Al-Barr. p14

text.text: أغبط النّاس عندي: رجل له دارٌ لا يجري عليه كراؤها، وله زوجة صالحة، قد رضيته ورضيها فهما راضيان بعيشهما، لا يعرفنا ولا نعرفه، فإنّه إن عرفنا وعرفناه أتعبنا ليله ونهاره، وأفسدنا دينه ودنياه.

text:
Bahjat al-Majālis by Ibn Abd Al-Barr. p20

Ziyād said: The happiest man to me is that who has a house that's not rented, and a righteous wife that is pleased with him, and he's pleased with her, so they're pleased with their lives. He doesn't know us [rulers], and we don't know him, because if he knew us and we knew him, we'd tire him all day and night, and we'd ruin his life and religion.

text.text:
باب ترويح القلوب وتنبيهها
قال عبد الله بن مسعود: كان رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وسلّم يتخوَّلنا بالموعظة مخافة السّآمة علينا.
وكان عليُّ بن أبي طالب يقول: إنّ هذه القلوب تملّ كما تملُّ الأبدان، فابتغوا لها طرائف الحكمة.
وقال عليٌّ رضي الله عنه: نبّه بالتفكّر قلبك، وجاف عن النوم جنبك، واتق الله ربّك.
قال أبو الدّرداء: إني لأستجمُّ قلبي بشيءٍ من اللهو، ليكون أقوى لي على الحقّ.
قال عبد الله بن مسعود: أريحوا القلوب، فإن القلب إذا أكره عمى.
وقال أيضاً: إنّ للقلوب شهوةً وإقبالا، وفترة وإدباراً، فخذوها عند شهواتها وإقبالها، وذروها عند فترتها وإدبارها.
كان يقال: الملالة تفسخ المودّة، وتولّد البغضة، وتنغّص اللّذة.
قال أرسطو طاليس: ينبغي للرّجل أن يعطي نفسه لذّتها في النهار ليكون ذلك عوناً لها على سائر يومه.
في صحف إبراهيم عليه السّلام: وعلى العاقل أن يكون له ثلاث ساعات: ساعةٌ يناجي فيها ربّه، وساعةٌ يحاسب فيها نفسه، وساعةٌ يخلّي فيها بين نفسه وبين لذاتها فيما يحلّ ويجمل، فإنّ هذه الساعة عونٌ له على سائر السّاعات.

text:
Summary: Allow yourself to do what pleases you, because your heart needs rest, so take some time to indulge in what you desire and is permissible and good.

Translation:

text.text:
Chapter: Giving the hearts rest and awakening them

ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said: The Messenger of Allah, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam would admonish us only from time to time, fearing that we might grow weary.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: These hearts get bored just as bodies do, so seek for them delightful insights.

He also said: Awaken your heart through reflection, keep your side away from sleep, and fear Allāh, your Rabb.

Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I give my heart rest with a bit of lawful amusement, so that it becomes stronger in upholding the truth.

Ibn Masʿūd said: Give the hearts rest, for when the heart is forced, it becomes blind.

He also said: Hearts have moments of desire and inclination, and moments of slackness and turning away. Engage them when they are eager and receptive, and leave them when they are weary and withdrawn.

It used to be said: Boredom breaks affection, gives rise to hatred, and spoils pleasure.

Aristotle said: A person should allow himself some enjoyment during the day, so that it helps him through the rest of it.

In the scriptures of Ibrāhīm ʿalayhi as-sallām: A sensible person should divide his time into three parts: a time to privately converse with his Lord, a time to hold himself to account, and a time to allow himself lawful and dignified enjoyment; for this part of time helps him with the others.

text: Bahjat al-Majālis by Ibn Abd Al-Barr. p20

text.text:
85 – Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, Abū ʿUmar Yūsuf bnu ʿAbdi Allāh an-Namarī

The Imām, the erudite scholar, the ḥāfiẓ of the Maghrib, Shaykh al-Islām: Abū ʿUmar Yūsuf bnu ʿAbdi Allāh bnu Muḥammad bnu ʿAbd al-Barr bnu ʿĀṣim an-Namarī, the Andalusian, the Cordoban, the Mālikī, author of outstanding works.

His birth was in the year 368 AH, in the month of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir.

He sought knowledge after the year 390 AH, met the senior scholars, lived to an advanced age, possessed a high isnād, students gathered around him in great numbers, he compiled and authored works, authenticated and declared weak (reports and narrators), his writings spread far and wide, and the scholars of his time submitted to his knowledge.

He missed hearing directly from his father, the imām Abū Muḥammad, for his father had died earlier in the year 380 AH; he had been a jurist, a devoted to worship and night prayer, and lived fifty years. He had studied fiqh under al-Tujībī, and heard from Aḥmad bnu Muṭrif and Abū ʿUmar bnu Ḥazm the historian.

Al-Ḥumaydī said: Abū ʿUmar was a jurist, a ḥāfiẓ, prolific, knowledgeable in the Qurʾānic readings, in legal disagreement, in the sciences of ḥadīth and narrators, received ḥadīth at an early age, and inclined in jurisprudence toward the views of ash-Shāfiʿī.

Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: There was no one in our land in ḥadīth like Qāsim bnu Muḥammad and Aḥmad bnu Khālid al-Jabbāb.
Then Abū ʿAlī said: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr was not beneath them, nor behind them. He was from an-Namir bnu Qāsiṭ; he sought knowledge and advanced in it, adhered closely to Abū ʿUmar Aḥmad bnu ʿAbd al-Malik the jurist, and to Abū al-Walīd bnu al-Faraḍī, persisted in the pursuit of ḥadīth and became deeply devoted to it, and excelled with an excellence by which he surpassed those before him among the men of al-Andalus.
Along with his leading mastery in the knowledge of transmitted reports and his insight into jurisprudence and meanings, he possessed a broad mastery of genealogy and historical reports. He departed from his homeland and resided for a time in the west, then moved to the eastern regions of al-Andalus, settling in Dāniyah, Valencia, and Shāṭiba, where he died.

More than one has mentioned that Abū ʿUmar held the judgeship of Lisbon for a while.

I say: He was an imām, devout, trustworthy, precise, a master scholar, profoundly learned, devoted to the Sunnah and adherence to it. At first he was, as has been said, an Atharī of Ẓāhirī inclination, then he became Mālikī, with a clear inclination in certain issues toward the jurisprudence of ash-Shāfiʿī. He was not denied this, for he had reached the rank of the mujtahid imāms. Whoever examines his writings will realize the vastness of his knowledge, the strength of his understanding, and the fluency of his intellect. Every person's statement may be accepted or rejected, except that of the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam;  yet if an imām errs in his ijtihād, it is not fitting for us to forget his virtues or obscure his knowledge. Rather, we seek forgiveness for him and excuse him.

Abū al-Qāsim bnu Bashkuwāl said: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr was the imām of his age and the unique figure of his era; his kunya was Abū ʿUmar.

Abū ʿAlī bnu Sukkarah said: I heard Abū al-Walīd al-Bājī say: There was none in al-Andalus like Abū ʿUmar bnu ʿAbd al-Barr in ḥadīth, and he was the most memorizing of the people of the Maghrib.

Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: Abū ʿUmar authored beneficial works on the Muwaṭṭaʾ, among them the book al-Tamhīd li-mā fī al-Muwaṭṭaʾ min al-Maʿānī wa-l-Asānīd, which he arranged according to the names of Mālik's shaykhs, in alphabetical order. It is an unprecedented book, consisting of seventy volumes.

I say: They are very large volumes.

Ibn Ḥazm said: I do not know anything in discourse on the fiqh of ḥadīth like it, how then could anything be better than it?

text.text:
He then produced the book al-Istithkār li-Math-hab ʿUlamāʾ al-Amṣār fīmā Taḍammanahu al-Muwaṭṭaʾ min Maʿānī ar-Raʾyi wa-l-Āthār, in which he explained the Muwaṭṭaʾ in its proper manner; and he compiled a great and beneficial book, al-Istīʿāb fī Asmāʾ al-Ṣaḥābah. He also authored Jāmiʿ Bayān al-ʿIlm wa-Faḍlih wa-mā Yanbaghī fī Riwayatihi wa-Ḥamlih, along his other works.

He was granted success in authorship, aided therein, and Allāh benefited people through his writings. Along with his leading mastery in transmitted knowledge and insight into jurisprudence and the meanings of ḥadīth, he possessed a wide mastery of genealogy and historical report.

A group mentioned that Abū ʿUmar held the judgeship of Lisbon and Santarém during the period of al-Muẓaffar bnu al-Afṭas.

Among Abū ʿUmar’s works are: al-Kāfī fī Math-hab Mālik in fifteen volumes; al-Iktifāʾ fī Qirāʾat Nāfiʿ wa-Abī ʿAmr; at-Taqaṣṣī fī Ikhtiṣār al-Muwaṭṭaʾ; al-Inbāh ʿan Qabāʾil ar-Ruwāt; al-Intiqāʾ li-Mathāhib ath-Thalāthati al-ʿUlamāʾ Mālik wa-Abī Ḥanīfah wa ash-Shāfiʿī; al-Bayān fī Tilāwat al-Qurʾān; al-Ajwibah al-Mūʿibah; al-Kunā; al-Maghāzī; al-Qaṣd wa l-Umam fī Nasab al-ʿArab wa l-ʿAjam; ash-Shawāhid fī Ithbāt Khabar al-Wāḥid; al-Inṣāf fī Asmāʾ Allāh; al-Farāʾiḍ; and Ashʿār Abī al-ʿAtāhiyah.

He lived ninety-five years.

Abū Dāwūd al-Muqriʾ said: Abū ʿUmar died on the night of Friday, at the end of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, in the year 463 AH, having completed ninety-five years and five days, may Allāh have mercy on him.

It is said that Abū ʿUmar was open and cordial with Abū Muḥammad bnu Ḥazm, and that Ibn Ḥazm learned the discipline of ḥadīth from him.

Our shaykh Abū ʿAbd Allāh bnu Abī al-Fatḥ said: Abū ʿUmar was the most knowledgeable person in al-Andalus regarding the Sunan, the transmitted reports, and the disagreements of the scholars of the regions. He said: In the early part of his life he followed the Ẓāhirī school for a long period, then returned to affirming analogical reasoning without imitating any particular individual, though he frequently inclined toward the school of ash-Shāfiʿī. Thus he said; but what is well-known is that he was a Mālikī.

I say: In the foundations of religion he was upon the path of the Salaf; he did not enter into kalām, but rather followed the traces of his shaykhs, may Allāh have mercy on them.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
This man is a gem.

The fact that he met Ibn Ḥazm is.....HUGE.
The fact that the two got along...is even...BIGGER.

Intellectual resonance!

The two men share a strong devotion to follow the Sunnah and hadīth, and follow the truth. They're both highly intellectual, smart, and possess incredible memory.

It's like two rare complex puzzle pieces fitting each other.

I don't think ath-Thahabī mentioned the two here in such way...spontaneously...

You could also, again, notice the fairness of ath-Thahabī, praising Ibn Abd Al-Barr, while affirming he's human who makes mistakes, and that his mistakes are nothing compared to his virtues.

One also benefits that, Ibn Abd Al-Barr is better than Ibn Ḥazm as he didn't drift into al-kalām and philosophy, which Ibn Ḥazm sadly did.

May Allāh have mercy on them all, and grant them al-Jannah.

I would love to meet such great men.

May Allāh not deprive us of such gift and blessing...Āmīn.

text_entities.text: Is placing the right hand over the left on the chest in prayer disliked (makrūh) by consensus?

By shaykh Sulaymān ar-Ruḥaylī, may Allah preserve him

A very detailed explanation covering all opinions and showing the origin of each.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
Summary (from my understanding):

* The closest to the Sunnah is placing the hands on the nukrah of the chest (the hollow area) or slightly below it.

* The ḥadīths supporting placing the hands below the navel are weak.

* The ḥadīths supporting placing the hands above the navel are weak, but slightly better than the previous ones.

* The ḥadīths supporting placing the hands on the chest are weak, but better than the two previous cases, and there are ḥadīths and reports that support it.

* Some ways of placing the right hand over the left only make sense if they are on the chest.

* This issue should not be a source of dispute, as there is no harm if people in the same mosque or congregation pray with their hands positioned as they believe correct.

* Those who claim it is disliked to place the hands on the chest are mistaken; their view is rejected. Many of them only refer to fiqh books.

* Placing the hands on the chest is mentioned in the fiqh of those before the four Imāms (Abu Ḥanīfah, Mālik, ash-Shāfi’ī, Ibn Ḥanbal).

* Al-Albāny, Ibn Bāz, and Ibn ’Uthaymeen, say the hands are to be placed on the chest.

May Allah reward the shaykh greatly for this beneficial clarification.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.text:
I appreciate shaykh Sulaymān ar-Ruḥaylī’s detailed explanations on many issues.

He shows no bias, respects all viewpoints, conveys information honestly, and presents each opinion along with its source and rationale.

Often, he provides details that I find only with him.

He also has a strong ability to clarify points of dispute.

Additionally, he excuses the Imāms if he thinks they're mistaken and emphasizes respecting them and not disparaging them.

It appears that he is far from following personal desires and shows sincerity in following the methodology of the Salaf and practicing his religion accordingly.

We ask Allah to keep him firm on the truth, protect him, and increase him in His bounty.

text:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
A Brief Overview of My Studies and Methodology

As I share knowledge publicly, I believe it is important to clarify my background and approach, so that those who benefit from my work may do so with understanding. The Salaf said: "This knowledge is religion, so choose carefully whom you take your knowledge from".

I began my journey as a seeker of knowledge independently, without realizing it. I was drawn to the tapes of al-Albāny, whose methodology I adopted after being convinced of its soundness. I also studied works of scholars such as Ibn Ḥazm, especially al-Muḥallā, which taught me structured reasoning, argumentation, and proper use of textual evidence.

I have read extensively about the history of the Salaf, as I realized my mind had been influenced by contemporary viewpoints. The friction between what I was learning and what I already knew was noticeable, and I am extremely grateful to Allāh for guiding me to the study of the Salaf, as it served as a remedy.

It took me two years, to be able to write something like that I wrote on the issue of photography, not realizing initially how deep it would be. In completing the work, I discovered numerous specious arguments and misconceptions, and I felt the need to build a reference, not just a simple refutation.

Through that research, I discovered the scholars of Yemen and that I was not alone in holding that photography is ḥarām. This was a great relief and a true treasure. I studied their works and lessons, and their methodology aligned with what I had learned from al-Albāny, which reassured me of their reliability. I benefited greatly from their fatāwā and guidance, which broadened my understanding of contemporary da’wah and the practical application of knowledge.

While I have not formally studied under a Salafi sheikh in person, I have consulted a few and sought their feedback on my work. AlḥamduliAllāh, this has helped me ensure that my understanding and output remain on the straight path.

My approach remains autodidactic; I continue to study independently, seeking guidance when necessary, always verifying knowledge through the Qurʾān, Sunnah, and the methodology of the Salaf.

It goes without saying that anyone who does not feel comfortable taking knowledge from me is free not to. Knowledge can be sought and benefited from in many ways.

text.text:
[مَسْأَلَةٌ الْمُجْتَهِدُ الْمُخْطِئُ أَفْضَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ الْمُقَلِّدِ الْمُصِيبِ]
108 - مَسْأَلَةٌ: وَالْمُجْتَهِدُ الْمُخْطِئُ أَفْضَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ الْمُقَلِّدِ الْمُصِيبِ. هَذَا فِي أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ خَاصَّةً، وَأَمَّا غَيْرُ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَلَا عُذْرَ لِلْمُجْتَهِدِ الْمُسْتَدِلِّ وَلَا لِلْمُقَلِّدِ، وَكِلَاهُمَا هَالِكٌ. بُرْهَانُ هَذَا مَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ آنِفًا بِإِسْنَادِهِ مِنْ قَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - «إذَا اجْتَهَدَ الْحَاكِمُ فَأَخْطَأَ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ» وَذَمَّ اللَّهُ التَّقْلِيدَ جُمْلَةً، فَالْمُقَلِّدُ عَاصٍ وَالْمُجْتَهِدُ مَأْجُورٌ، وَلَيْسَ مَنْ اتَّبَعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - مُقَلِّدًا لِأَنَّهُ فَعَلَ مَا أَمَرَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِهِ. وَإِنَّمَا الْمُقَلِّدُ مَنْ اتَّبَعَ مَنْ دُونَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - لِأَنَّهُ فَعَلَ مَا لَمْ يَأْمُرْهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِهِ وَأَمَّا غَيْرُ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ: {وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإِسْلامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ} [آل عمران: 85]

[Masʾalah: To Allāh, Exalted is He, The Erring Mujtahid Is Superior Than a Correct Imitator

108 — masʾalah: the erring mujtahid is superior to Allāh, Exalted is He, than the correct muqallid (imitator). This applies specifically to the people of Islām. As for those outside Islām, there is no excuse—neither for the mujtahid who engages in inferential reasoning nor for the imitator; both are doomed.

The proof of this is what we previously cited, with its chain of transmission (isnād), from the statement of the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam:
“If a judge exercises ijtihād and errs, he has one reward”.
Moreover, Allāh has categorically condemned taqlīd (imitation). Thus, the muqallid is disobedient, whereas the mujtahid is rewarded.
And one who follows the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, is not a muqallid, because he has done what Allāh, Exalted is He, commanded him to do. Rather, a muqallid is one who follows someone other than the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, for he has done what Allāh, Exalted is He, did not command him to do.
As for those outside Islām, Allāh, Exalted is He, says:
“Whoever seeks a religion other than Islām, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers” [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]

108 - مَسْأَلَةٌ: وَالْمُجْتَهِدُ الْمُخْطِئُ أَفْضَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ الْمُقَلِّدِ الْمُصِيبِ. هَذَا فِي أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ خَاصَّةً، وَأَمَّا غَيْرُ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَلَا عُذْرَ لِلْمُجْتَهِدِ الْمُسْتَدِلِّ وَلَا لِلْمُقَلِّدِ، وَكِلَاهُمَا هَالِكٌ. بُرْهَانُ هَذَا مَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ آنِفًا بِإِسْنَادِهِ مِنْ قَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - «إذَا اجْتَهَدَ الْحَاكِمُ فَأَخْطَأَ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ» وَذَمَّ اللَّهُ التَّقْلِيدَ جُمْلَةً، فَالْمُقَلِّدُ عَاصٍ وَالْمُجْتَهِدُ مَأْجُورٌ، وَلَيْسَ مَنْ اتَّبَعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - مُقَلِّدًا لِأَنَّهُ فَعَلَ مَا أَمَرَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِهِ. وَإِنَّمَا الْمُقَلِّدُ مَنْ اتَّبَعَ مَنْ دُونَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - لِأَنَّهُ فَعَلَ مَا لَمْ يَأْمُرْهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِهِ وَأَمَّا غَيْرُ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ: {وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإِسْلامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ} [آل عمران: 85]

[Masʾalah: To Allāh, Exalted is He, The Erring Mujtahid Is Superior Than a Correct Imitator

108 — masʾalah: the erring mujtahid is superior to Allāh, Exalted is He, than the correct muqallid (imitator). This applies specifically to the people of Islām. As for those outside Islām, there is no excuse—neither for the mujtahid who engages in inferential reasoning nor for the imitator; both are doomed.

The proof of this is what we previously cited, with its chain of transmission (isnād), from the statement of the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam:
“If a judge exercises ijtihād and errs, he has one reward”.
Moreover, Allāh has categorically condemned taqlīd (imitation). Thus, the muqallid is disobedient, whereas the mujtahid is rewarded.
And one who follows the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, is not a muqallid, because he has done what Allāh, Exalted is He, commanded him to do. Rather, a muqallid is one who follows someone other than the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, for he has done what Allāh, Exalted is He, did not command him to do.
As for those outside Islām, Allāh, Exalted is He, says:
“Whoever seeks a religion other than Islām, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers” [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]
— Ibn Ḥazm, al-Muḥallā bi’l-Āthār, 1:88

text.text: وَالِاجْتِهَادُ إنَّمَا مَعْنَاهُ بُلُوغُ الْجَهْدِ فِي طَلَبِ دِينِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الَّذِي أَوْجَبَهُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ، وَبِالضَّرُورَةِ يَدْرِي كُلُّ ذِي حِسٍّ سَلِيمٍ أَنَّ الْمُسْلِمَ لَا يَكُونُ مُسْلِمًا إلَّا حَتَّى يُقِرَّ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى إلَهُهُ لَا إلَهَ غَيْرُهُ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا هُوَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - بِهَذَا الدِّينِ إلَيْهِ وَإِلَى غَيْرِهِ

And ijtihād simply means exerting effort in seeking the religion of Allāh, Exalted is He, which He has made obligatory upon His servants. And it is necessarily known to anyone of sound intellect that a Muslim cannot be a Muslim except by acknowledging that Allāh, Exalted is He, is their only god, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, to him, and to others.

text:
— Ibn Ḥazm, al-Muḥallā bi’l-Āthār, 1:86

Here Ibn Ḥazm destroys the specious argument of some of those who call to taqlīd and claim ijtihād is rare or beyond ordinary obligation.

He clarifies that ijtihād is graded, each person exercises it according to their capacity; it is not a single absolute level.

messages.text:
What poisons family relations is not disagreement, but the lack of frankness that turns into backbiting.

We don’t have the courage to sit with a family member and speak plainly about what troubles us. Instead, we speak about them, not to them, from a posture of moral superiority.

Face to face: warmth, smiles, exaggerated kindness.

The moment they leave: mockery, complaints, character assassination.
This isn’t politeness. It’s fear. Outright stupidity.

It’s cowardice dressed as manners. 

Frankness requires risk. Backbiting is cheap and feels righteous. So people outsource courage to gossip and call it “concern”.

That fake warmth to the face, knives out behind the back, is what ruins relationships, makes them hollow, and kills the ability to cooperate and help each other learn and be better.

Apply the same to other types of relationships.
Don't tip toe around what you want to say, and don't stay around those who do, and don't stay around those who can't take no-tip-toeing.
Yes it's a small circle.

text.text: Advice and Warning to Those Who Are Lax Regarding Photography

text:
I've observed that some use images of senior scholars, placing on them sentimental phrases, and justify this by obscuring the face.

This is a corrupt practice; these images were originally produced in sin, so using them is an acknowledgment of the wrong, a habituation of the general public to it, and a step of the steps of Shayṭān.

Had the photographer feared Allāh, the image would never have been taken in the first place.

Is it fitting, then, that the fruit of his sin be made a medium for daʿwah?

Would any of you stand before scholars and photograph them from the neck down, in their presence?

The Prophet ﷺ commanded that images acquired in ignorance of the ruling be obliterated, in order to get rid of them.

This, in no way, justifies seeking out images, then obscuring them, then using them in daʿwah.

This is neither honoring the scholars, nor following the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ and the Salaf.

Ask yourselves: would the scholar depicted consent to a post showing his body with his head scribbled over or distorted in strange shapes?

messages.title: تصوير ما دون الرأس
text:
Question: Some people are lax regarding photography and take pictures of the body without the head. They say they do so for remembrance. What is the ruling on this?

Answer (Shaykh Yaḥyā ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥajūrī): Like a shepherd grazing around a protected sanctuary (ḥimā), about to graze inside it.
Don't do this.
That is, photographing this or that, and some covering the head and photographing the body: avoid it.

Beings with souls are not to be photographed. Photograph trees and that which has no soul; this is permissible.

As for beings with souls, whether human or otherwise, they are not to be photographed, due to the prohibition against it.

Source:

text.text:
كَانَتْ بيْنَ أبِي بَكْرٍ وعُمَرَ مُحَاوَرَةٌ، فأغْضَبَ أبو بَكْرٍ عُمَرَ فَانْصَرَفَ عنْه عُمَرُ مُغْضَبًا، فَاتَّبَعَهُ أبو بَكْرٍ يَسْأَلُهُ أنْ يَسْتَغْفِرَ له، فَلَمْ يَفْعَلْ حتَّى أغْلَقَ بَابَهُ في وجْهِهِ، فأقْبَلَ أبو بَكْرٍ إلى رَسولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ، فَقالَ أبو الدَّرْدَاءِ ونَحْنُ عِنْدَهُ: فَقالَ رَسولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ: أمَّا صَاحِبُكُمْ هذا فقَدْ غَامَرَ قالَ: ونَدِمَ عُمَرُ علَى ما كانَ منه، فأقْبَلَ حتَّى سَلَّمَ وجَلَسَ إلى النبيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ، وقَصَّ علَى رَسولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ الخَبَرَ، قالَ أبو الدَّرْدَاءِ: وغَضِبَ رَسولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ، وجَعَلَ أبو بَكْرٍ يقولُ: واللَّهِ يا رَسولَ اللَّهِ لَأَنَا كُنْتُ أظْلَمَ، فَقالَ رَسولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ: هلْ أنتُمْ تَارِكُونَ لي صَاحِبِي، هلْ أنتُمْ تَارِكُونَ لي صَاحِبِي، إنِّي قُلتُ: يا أيُّها النَّاسُ، إنِّي رَسولُ اللَّهِ إلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا، فَقُلتُمْ: كَذَبْتَ، وقالَ أبو بَكْرٍ: صَدَقْتَ قالَ أبو عبدِ اللَّهِ: غَامَرَ: سَبَقَ بالخَيْرِ.
صحيح البخاري 4640

A discussion arose between Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. Abū Bakr angered ʿUmar, and ʿUmar walked away in anger. Abū Bakr followed him, asking him to seek forgiveness for him on his behalf, but ʿUmar refused, eventually closing the door in his face.

Abū Bakr then went to the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ. Abū ad-Dardāʾ said—while we were with him—the Prophet ﷺ remarked:
“As for this companion of yours, he has taken the lead in righteousness”.

ʿUmar, regretting what he had done, came, greeted the Prophet ﷺ, sat before him, and recounted the matter.

Abū ad-Dardāʾ said: the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ became angry, and Abū Bakr said:
“By Allāh, O Messenger of Allāh, I was more at fault”.

The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ then said:
“Will you not leave my companion alone? Will you not leave my companion alone? I said, ‘O people, I am the Messenger of Allāh to you all’, and you said, ‘You're lying’, while Abū Bakr said, ‘You have spoken the truth’”.

Saḥeeḥ Al-Bukhārī 4640

text:
Look at the amount of frankness in this incidence:
* They disagreed openly.
* Umar expressed anger to Abu Bakr
* Abu Bakr kept following Umar asking him to seek forgiveness for him on his behalf. He confessed to being in the wrong.
* Umar being frank about not being able to forgive. He outright refused.
* Abu Bakr didn't leave it there, he went to the Prophet ﷺ, whose the father to all believers. Abu Bakr was not happy about upsetting his friend Umar.
* Umar after calming down and realizing he should've forgiven him. He's frank with himself.
* Umar didn't stop there, he too went to the Prophet ﷺ, he knew it's not right to keep his friend Abu Bakr is such worry and stress, even though he knew he will have to admit being wrong.
* The Prophet ﷺ being frank and warning everyone to not treat Abu Bakr like they treat everyone else, even if he is mistaken, for his high status and precedence in Islām outweigh such matters.

These two companions are the best of mankind after the prophets. Look how they treat each other. Having a solid and strong love relationship doesn't mean no fighting or anger, that's a very wrong mindset to have.

We have that mindset, and look where it got us.

* Abu Bakr didn't leave it there, he went to the Prophet ﷺ, whose the father to all believers. Abu Bakr was not happy about upsetting his friend Umar.
* Umar after calming down and realizing he should've forgiven him. He's frank with himself.
* Umar didn't stop there, he too went to the Prophet ﷺ, he knew it's not right to keep his friend Abu Bakr is such worry and stress, even though he knew he will have to admit being wrong.
* The Prophet ﷺ being frank and warning everyone to not treat Abu Bakr like they treat everyone else, even if he is mistaken, for his high status and precedence in Islām outweigh such matters.

These two companions are the best of mankind after the prophets. Look how they treat each other. Having a solid and strong love relationship doesn't mean no fighting or anger, that's a very wrong mindset to have.

We have that mindset, and look where it got us.

text.text: An Important Benefit: Combining the Evidences

text:
There is an important principle, which is: In matters of religion, it is necessary to combine all the evidences.
Do not take some evidences and leave others.

Example:

The ḥadīths in which it is mentioned:
“Whoever dies saying Lā ilāha illā Allāh…” must be combined with other ḥadīths that restricted it with knowledge, sincerity, and certainty.

Allāh, Exalted is He, said:
{ أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ }
"Then do you believe in a part of the Scripture and reject the rest?" [Al-Baqarah: 85]

text.text:
س (371) اذْكُرْ بَعْضَ أَسْمَاءِ جَهَنَّمَ؟
جـ (371) الْ‍حُطَمَةُ، وَلَظَى، وَسَقَرُ، وَالْ‍هَاوِيَةُ، وَالسَّعِيرُ.

Q (371) Mention some of the names of Jahannam.
A (371) Al-Ḥuṭamah (The Crusher), Laẓā (The Blaze), Saqar (The Scorching Fire), al-Hāwiyah (The Pit), as-Saʿīr (The Inferno).

text: Source: Kanz Al-Atfāl (Tr. Al-Qaddārī)

:

Al-Ḥuṭamah → The Crusher
It crushes what gets thrown into it and destroys it.

Laẓā → The Blaze
Intense, the hottest of all flames.

Saqar → The Scorching Fire
Extreme heat that inflicts unbearable pain.

Al-Hāwiyah → The Pit
Stark, abyssal; those cast into it keep falling for as long as Allāh wills.

As-Saʿīr → The Inferno
Vast, raging, and terrifying.

: Do not depict Jahannam with images. Allāh chose to describe it in words alone, and the salaf relied on these descriptions.
That is sufficient to make us tremble, fear His Fire, and instill awe, warning, and humility before Allāh.

Relying on images suggests that one may feel words alone are not enough to convey the terror of the Fire.

If words were truly enough, no extra effort would be needed. Spending time and energy on images either misses the point of Allāh's choice, or is wasted effort. Either way, it is wrong—the first case being far more serious.

What was enough for the salaf is enough for us. Modern ease of creating images does not nullify this principle.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
text:
One might think, that, if Jahannam is that extreme, wouldn't people just evaporate as soon they get any close to it?

The answer is:

text.text:
س (374) كَمْ عِظَمُ جِلْدِ الْكَافِرِ فِي النَّارِ وَضِرْسِهِ؟
جـ (374) عِظَمُ جِلْدِهِ مَسِيرَةُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ، وَضِرْسُهُ مِثْلُ جَبَلِ أُحُدٍ.

Q (374) How large are the skin and molar tooth of a disbeliever in the Fire?
A (374) The breadth of his skin will span a three-day journey, and his molar tooth will be as large as Mount Uḥud.

text:
Yes, it'll have more fuel than you think, so that the kuffār suffer and don't evaporate so quickly.

Do you realize how far are we from comprehending Jahannam?
And you don't have to fully grasp how horrible it is, the little amount you do comprehend is enough, as Allāh allowed us to understand enough to be afraid of it. If we did fully grasp its severity, no one would even think about disobeying Allāh, and that would not be a test, which worldly life is.

May Allāh protect us and you all from such horrible destiny, and grant us al-Jannah without tasting any torment in Jahannam.

والله المستعان.

text: «صحيح الترغيب والترهيب» (3/ 472):

text.text:
3669 - (4) [حسن] وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
"لمّا خلَق الله الجنَّة والنارَ، أرسلَ جبريلَ إلى الجنَّةِ فقال: انظرْ إليْها وإلى ما أعَددْتُ لأَهْلِها فيها، قال: فجاءَ فنظَر إليها وإلى ما أعدَّ الله لأَهْلِها فيها، قال: فرجَع إليْهِ، قال: وعِزَّتِكَ! لا يَسْمَعُ بها أحَدٌ إلا دخَلها! فأمَر بها فَحُفَّتْ بالمكَارِه. فقال: ارْجعْ إليْها فانْظُر إلى ما أعَددْتُ لأَهْلها فيها. قال: فرجَع إليها فإذا هِيَ قد ‌حُفَّتْ ‌بالمكارِه، فرجَع إليه فقال: وعِزَّتِكَ! لقد خِفتُ أنْ لا يَدْخُلَها أحَدٌ! وقال: اذْهَبْ إلى النارِ فانْظُرْ إليْها وإلى ما أعَدَدْتُ لأَهْلِها فيها، قال: فنظَر إليها، فإذا هي يَرْكَبُ بعضها بعضاً، فرجعَ إليه فقال: وعِزَّتِكَ لا يسمَعُ بها أحدٌ فيدْخُلَها، فأمَر بها فحُفَّتْ بالشَّهواتِ، فقال: ارْجعْ إليها، فرجَع إليها، فقال: وعِزَّتِك! لقد خَشيتُ أنْ لا يَنْجُوَ منها أحَدٌ إلا دخَلَها".
رواه أبو داود والنسائي، والترمذي واللفظ له، وقال:
"حديث حسن صحيح".

text: Ṣaḥīḥ at-Targhīb wa at-Tarhīb (3/472):

text.text:
3669 – (4) [Ḥasan]

On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

“When Allāh created al-Jannah and the Fire, He sent Jibrīl to al-Jannah and said: ‘Look at it and at what I have prepared therein for its inhabitants’.
He came to it and looked at it and at what Allāh had prepared therein for its inhabitants, then he returned to Him and said: ‘By Your Might! No one will hear of it except that he will enter it’.
So He commanded that it be surrounded by hardships.
He said: ‘Return to it and look at what I have prepared therein for its inhabitants’.
He returned to it and found that it had been surrounded by hardships. He returned to Him and said: ‘By Your Might! I fear that no one will enter it’.
Then He said: ‘Go to the Fire and look at it and at what I have prepared therein for its inhabitants’.
He looked at it, and behold—it was piled one upon another. He returned to Him and said: ‘By Your Might! No one will hear of it and then enter it’.
So He commanded that it be surrounded by desires.
He said: ‘Return to it’.
He returned to it and said: ‘By Your Might! I fear that none will be saved from it except that he will enter it’”.

Reported by Abū Dāwūd, an-Nasāʾī, and at-Tirmithī (this is his wording), who said:
“A ḥadīth that is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ”.

text: "ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ": Meaning: “This report is reliable and acceptable, though not at the highest authenticity standards”.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري

text.text: On Those Who Claim Muslims Must Change

text:
Some say: "Muslims must adapt, times change, we need more liberty, technology. We've seen other societies".

But, Islām doesn’t bend because tools change or tastes shift. The principles remain constant, and the Sharīʿah continues to govern action, intention, and limits.

New technologies or ideas do not create new values; they instead should reveal how well we understand and apply timeless guidance.
Those claims raise a clear banner: a public confession of failure to understand Islām.

The confusion arises when weak minds encounter new cases (nawāzil) and mistake them for the foundations (qawāʿid), and that is not Islām failing, it is a failure of understanding.

Like someone unfamiliar with mathematics thinking formulas break when numbers grow or expressions change form; what changes are the circumstances, not the underlying truth.

Advancement in tools does not alter human nature, for desires, responsibilities, sin, and morality remain constant. The Sharīʿah addresses these realities, not fleeting trends.

A sound mind would not discard change, nor would it discard Islām. It integrates new realities and subjects them to what Islām already guides.

Real scholarship requires discipline, restraint, humility, and the ability to engage abstract principles without panic.

A weak mind fails at every one of these. It relies on superficial observation, and pretends it's insight, because that's the quickest route.

The work of serious scholars exposes how weak that reasoning is, how flawed and hollow.

History provides examples:
* Ahl al-Ḥadīth were initially weak against Ahl ar-Ra’y (People of Opinion), until ash-Shāfiʿī mastered the methods they claimed to master, and established correct fiqh.
* Ibn Ḥazm challenged blind taqlīd and faulty reasoning.
* Ibn Taymiyyah dismantled the ground from beneath philosophy.

Change is inevitable in tools, methods, and societies, but the core of Islām is constant. If one cannot understand both, they have no business nullifying either.

text:
Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn رحمه الله said:

“

text.text: What is lacking in our knowledge is that we do not apply what we have learned to our conduct.

text: For the most part, we only know the legal ruling, but as for putting it into practice, that is very little, we ask Allāh to deal with us with His pardon.

text.text: The benefit of knowledge lies in its practical application

text: , such that the effect of knowledge is seen on a person’s face, his behavior, his manners, his worship, his dignity, his reverence for Allāh, and other such things.

text.text: Mere theoretical matters are not the real aim of knowledge; rather, the benefit of knowledge is to reap its fruits.

text: And how often do you find from the common folk, unlearned person who has more humility before Allāh ﷻ, more awareness of Him, better conduct, character, and worship than many a student of knowledge.”

text_entities.text: Practical Application of Knowledge!

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn رحمه الله said:

“
What is lacking in our knowledge is that we do not apply what we have learned to our conduct.
For the most part, we only know the legal ruling, but as for putting it into practice, that is very little, we ask Allāh to deal with us with His pardon.
The benefit of knowledge lies in its practical application
, such that the effect of knowledge is seen on a person’s face, his behavior, his manners, his worship, his dignity, his reverence for Allāh, and other such things.
This is what truly matters.
Mere theoretical matters are not the real aim of knowledge; rather, the benefit of knowledge is to reap its fruits.
And how often do you find from the common folk, unlearned person who has more humility before Allāh ﷻ, more awareness of Him, better conduct, character, and worship than many a student of knowledge.”
[Ash-Sharḥ al-Mumtiʿ (7/166)]

messages.text:
Something that helps making this happen is studying only what matters to you at the moment, what you need in your actual life currently, so you could live according to what Allāh wants from us.

Don't go about seeking knowledge like you're pursuing an academic diploma. Please.

You'll just end up piling information. That's how theory overwhelms practice. Which is one of the reasons I hate academic systems.

Remember how the companions learned 10 āyāt at once.

Somehow, almost everyone simply ignores that method, and just goes about memorizing so many things and delving into issues that they're far from needing them anytime soon.

Perhaps that's why we have a character crisis. Too much theory hardens the heart, and poofs one up like a balloon.

It's sad. But it is true.

messages.text:
Be warned and do not be among those who when Allah relieves him from a hardship he says: "The affair was easier than I thought, it wasn't that difficult, I over exaggerated the issue".. and the likes of this speech which indicate to the ingratitude of the servant and his denial of the blessings of Allah.


حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ، ثنا عَوْنُ بْنُ مُوسَى، سَمِعْتُ بَكْرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْمُزَنِيَّ، يَقُولُ: " يَنْزِلُ بِالْعَبْدِ الْأَمْرُ فَيَدْعُو فَيَصْرِفُهُ عَنْهُ، فَيَأْتِيهِ الشَّيْطَانُ فَيُضْعِفُ شُكْرَهُ، فَيَقُولُ: إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كَانَ أَيْسَرَ مِمَّا تَذْهَبُ إِلَيْهِ."

Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us: 'Awn ibn Musa narrated to us: I heard Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani saying: 'A matter befalls a servant, so he supplicates (to Allah) and He diverts it from him. Then Shaytān comes to him and weakens his gratitude, saying: Indeed, the matter was simpler than you think.'"

"Kitāb Ash-shukr"
Ibn Abi Ad-dunyā

It helps understand this if you imagine someone doing you a big favor and saving you from big trouble.

Then, as you feel freedom and relief, you turn to the one who saved you, and say:
"Oh wow, I guess I was just exaggerating that thingy haha. Humans

love dramatising. But thanks anyway man, appreciate it".

Now imagine acting this way towards Allāh.

But even that list uses "dh" for both "ذ" and "ظ".

Also, "th" is naturally used for both "ث" and "ذ".

My approach is more "English reader intuition", not the standard.

So, so far, I'll stick to this opinion of mine.

text:
Also:

From Merriam-Webster, the definition of "worthy":

text.text:
adjective
wor·​thy
 | \ ˈwər-t͟hē  \
wor​thi​er; wor​thi​est

Definition (Entry 1 of 2)

1
a: having worth or value : estimable//a worthy cause
b: honorable, meritorious
//worthy candidates

2: having sufficient worth or importance
//worthy to be remembered

text:
So, "worthy" is enough. Adding "in truth" is redundant.

If you don't mention "in truth", it's still perfectly correct, because nothing but Allāh is worthy of worship.

No one can say: X is worthy of worship, but not in truth.

That's just not how English works.

It's not wrong to add "in truth", technically, but it causes redundancy. Redundancy is not good.

Either use "worthy" or "in truth", not both. Please.

text: Some have said:

text.text:
We used to live the most beautiful moments without photographing them;
now we photograph the most beautiful moments without living them.

text:
I say: This is an admonition even for those whom Allah has guided to recognize the prohibition of depicting animate beings.

Put that phone aside. Refrain from photographing this and that, and from publishing this and that.

Especially if you are among those who call to Allah, because by doing this you accustom people to waving their phones everywhere:
“Shaykh so-and-so does this; don't be so strict akhi”.

How many times has a shaykh photographed animate beings without paying attention, and then published it?

Why place yourself in such a position?

It is because you do not truly realize prohibition of tasweer and its severity, even if you think you do, whoever you may be.

What sufficed those before you, and sufficed our senior scholars, should suffice you as well.
We do not know of them such expansion in this matter, nor the spreading of it. We do not see this as part of the bearing (samt—سمت) of the people of knowledge and virtue.

----

text.text:
bearing (noun)
1: the manner in which one behaves or comports oneself : the manner in which one bears oneself
Example: a man of dignified bearing

messages.text:
Starting from 13:32, the shaykh begins discussing the practice of stating and insisting on formal definitions, and he encourages using examples instead.

He notes that this practice is an influence of philosophers on grammarians and uṣūl scholars, and it is not something Arabs traditionally did.

Example: In Sibawayh’s book, one does not find the many definitions that later scholars present.

والحمد لله حمدا كثيرا
for this precious benefit.

May Allāh have mercy on Ibn Taymiyyah.

text: بسم الله الرحمـٰن الرحيم

text.text:
من تزوج امرأة تلبس النقاب والقفاز ولا تتفرج على التلفاز وإلى أهل الحق تنحاز ولا تذهب إلى الحمام ولا تكثر الملام فقد حاز على امرأة الأحلام
 [الإمام الألمعي ص٢٤٨]

Whoever marries a woman who wears a niqab and gloves, doesn't watch television, sides with the righteous, doesn't go to the hammām (public saunas/pools), and doesn't complain excessively, has found the woman of dreams.
[Al-imām Al-Almaʿi p.248]

text:
A very widespread quote attributed to imām Al-wādiʿi رحمه الله.

When I opened the book Al-imām Al-Almaʿi and went through it I did not find a single line of this quote mentioned, and in page 248 the only thing he said about women is:

"النِّساء السّلفيات أغلى من الذهب الأحمر"
"Salafi women are more precious than red gold"

but that's it.

I tried to find another source for this quote or proof that he said it but none at all. 

I asked Shaykha Umm Salama wife of Shaykh Muqbil if he really said that and this was her response:

"Shaykh al-Wādiʿī was not someone who used rhymed, ornate speech or embellished his words. So I do not think this is his speech at all. And since you searched in the book and did not find it, then it would be something falsely attributed to him."

This really highlights the importance of mentioning and checking the sources of whatever we share or read.

It is important that when we quote someone we make sure it is not falsely attributed to them, and when we do know who the quote belongs to then it is important we mention so and this is from الأمانة العِلمية (ʿilm integrity) and is how our deen is preserved.

Imām Muḥammad bin sīrīn said:
"إِنَّ هَذَا الْعِلْمَ دِينٌ. فَانْظُرُوا عَمَّنْ تَأْخُذُونَ دِينَكُمْ."
"Indeed this knowledge is religion, so look to whom you take your religion from."
[Saḥiḥ Muslim 1/14]

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 
 "كفى بِالْمَرْءِ كَذِبًا أَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ".
“It is enough of a lie for a person to repeat everything he hears.”
[Saḥiḥ Muslim 1/10]

So fear Allāh in what you share, especially during a time when tribulations are like pieces of a dark night, when truth and falsehood have mixed we must strive to seek the truth and differentiate it.

text.text:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

«من تزوّج امرأة تلبس النقاب والقفاز، ولا تتفرّج على التلفاز، وإلى أهل الحق تنحاز، ولا تذهب إلى الحمّام، ولا تُكثر الملام، فقد حاز على امرأة الأحلام».
[الإمام الألمعي ص 248]

هذه مقولة منتشرة جدًّا تُنسب إلى الإمام الوادعي رحمه الله.

وعندما فتحتُ كتاب الإمام الألمعي واطّلعتُ عليه، لم أجد سطرًا واحدًا من هذه المقولة، ولا يوجد في الصفحة 248 قول له عن النساء إلا:
«النِّساء السلفيّات أغلى من الذهب الأحمر».
ولا شيء غير ذلك.

حاولتُ البحث عن مصدر آخر لهذه المقولة أو دليل على أنه قالها، فلم أجد شيئًا أبدًا.

ثم سألتُ الشيخة أم سلمة زوجة الشيخ مقبل رحمه الله: هل قال الشيخ هذا الكلام؟ فكان جوابها:
«لم يكن الشيخ الوادعي ممن يسجع الكلام وينمقه، فلا أظن أن هذا من كلامه أبدا. وبما أنك بحثت في الكتاب ولم تجديه، فسيكون مكذوبا عليه».

وهذا يبيّن بوضوح أهمية ذِكر المصادر والتحقق منها لكل ما ننشر أو نقرأ. فمن المهم عند نقل كلام أحد أن نتأكد من صحة نسبته إليه، وإذا عُرف قائله وجب ذِكره، وهذا من الأمانة العلمية، وبهذا يُحفظ ديننا.

قال الإمام محمد بن سيرين رحمه الله:
«إِنَّ هَذَا الْعِلْمَ دِينٌ، فَانْظُرُوا عَمَّنْ تَأْخُذُونَ دِينَكُمْ».
[صحيح مسلم 1 / 14]

وقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«كفى بالمرء كذبًا أن يُحدّث بكل ما سمع».
[صحيح مسلم 1 / 10]

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

«من تزوّج امرأة تلبس النقاب والقفاز، ولا تتفرّج على التلفاز، وإلى أهل الحق تنحاز، ولا تذهب إلى الحمّام، ولا تُكثر الملام، فقد حاز على امرأة الأحلام».
[الإمام الألمعي ص 248]

هذه مقولة منتشرة جدًّا تُنسب إلى الإمام الوادعي رحمه الله.

وعندما فتحتُ كتاب الإمام الألمعي واطّلعتُ عليه، لم أجد سطرًا واحدًا من هذه المقولة، ولا يوجد في الصفحة 248 قول له عن النساء إلا:
«النِّساء السلفيّات أغلى من الذهب الأحمر».
ولا شيء غير ذلك.

حاولتُ البحث عن مصدر آخر لهذه المقولة أو دليل على أنه قالها، فلم أجد شيئًا أبدًا.

ثم سألتُ الشيخة أم سلمة زوجة الشيخ مقبل رحمه الله: هل قال الشيخ هذا الكلام؟ فكان جوابها:
«لم يكن الشيخ الوادعي ممن يسجع الكلام وينمقه، فلا أظن أن هذا من كلامه أبدا. وبما أنك بحثت في الكتاب ولم تجديه، فسيكون مكذوبا عليه».

وهذا يبيّن بوضوح أهمية ذِكر المصادر والتحقق منها لكل ما ننشر أو نقرأ. فمن المهم عند نقل كلام أحد أن نتأكد من صحة نسبته إليه، وإذا عُرف قائله وجب ذِكره، وهذا من الأمانة العلمية، وبهذا يُحفظ ديننا.

قال الإمام محمد بن سيرين رحمه الله:
«إِنَّ هَذَا الْعِلْمَ دِينٌ، فَانْظُرُوا عَمَّنْ تَأْخُذُونَ دِينَكُمْ».
[صحيح مسلم 1 / 14]

وقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«كفى بالمرء كذبًا أن يُحدّث بكل ما سمع».
[صحيح مسلم 1 / 10]

فاتقوا الله فيما تنشرون، لا سيما في زمنٍ صارت فيه الفتن كقطع الليل المظلم، واختلط فيه الحق بالباطل، فيجب علينا أن نجتهد في طلب الحق والتمييز بينه وبين غيره.

— كتبته أمُّ عبد الرحمن السودانية، غفر الله لها

text.text: A Piece Of Advice regarding the issue of taswīr

text:
Go easy on common folks regarding the issue if tasweer.

There's a lot of falsehood out there, and the whole world has no issue with using and making pictures.

It takes a considerable amount of courage to go against all of that, and join the isolated island of truth.

If Allāh has not granted you tawfeeq and guidance, you'd be out there sharing memes and watching funny videos.

It's quite heavy to accept that tasweer of animate beings is ḥarām, so do your best to make your advice and approach as tolerable and easy as you could.

Pretend you want to keep a thin cord attached between you and them. They're already pulling so hard, so don't mirror that. Go soft. (Wisdom benefited from a narration from Mu’āwiyah, may Allāh be pleased with him. Not sure if authentic, but the meaning is correct).

With that said, I feel optimistic, that this scourge will soon meet its demise, which is why I named my book what means: The Rising of the Dawn's Light, Upon the Issue of Photography in Its Darkest Night.

Meaning, inshaa'Allah, this book is the start of fighting the darkness of this issue, and raising awareness about it.

والله المستعان.

---
