text: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

text.text: What does it mean to "do your best"?

text:
Does it mean pushing yourself to the maximum? More effort? More time? More exhaustion? Should we assume the closer we are to collapse, the closer we are to sincerity?

This assumption is not only wrong. It is dangerous.

Because there are two very different things people call "their best".

The first is your

. The absolute most you can extract from yourself in a moment. It ignores tomorrow. It ignores recovery. It ignores limits.

It is intense.

Intensity feels meaningful. It gives the ego something to admire.

But it does not last.

The second is your

. This is the effort you can return to again and again. It respects your human limits. It protects continuity. It is stable.
This is the real measure.

Because what transforms you is not what you can do once. It is what you can keep doing.

A person may push himself to an extreme level of worship, study, or effort for a week. He sleeps less. He strains himself. He feels sincere.

Then:
His body weakens.
His mind resists.
He slows down.

It does not stop there.

He begins to think:
"Why can't I do what I was doing before?"
"Have I become lazy?"
"Has Allāh deprived me?"

He mistakes his collapse for a spiritual failure, when in reality it was a structural failure.

He built something he was never meant to sustain.

A quiet trap.

The ego pushes you into extremes, and when you inevitably fall, it accuses you. 

Because you stopped satisfying it.

But real devotion is not proven by peaks.
It is proven by continuity.
Consistency is what reshapes you.
The body adapts to repeated action. The brain strengthens pathways it uses often.
The soul settles into what it practices regularly.

This is how change becomes permanent.

Sustainable effort is not less.
It is superior. Because it survives.

It protects you from burnout. It protects you from despair. It protects you from the illusion that sincerity must destroy you.

Doing your best does not mean squeezing out the maximum possible effort today.

It means offering the best effort you can continue to offer.

It means understanding that you are not built for constant extremes.

You are built for persistence.

Allāh does not burden you beyond the limits He created you with.

When you understand this, anxiety loses its voice.
You stop panicking when your energy fluctuates.
You stop interpreting normal human variation as spiritual failure.

You focus on staying in motion.
Even slowly.
Even quietly.

Because real growth happens quietly.

A reminder for myself, then, to you, really.

—Abū Sahl ʿAbdurraḥmān al-Qaddārī

messages.text:
Wallāhi, the shaykh's voice here is far more beautiful, clear, pure, natural, and pleasing.

Why are we doing this, O brothers of faith?

Have you considered that you are altering an act of worship that Allāh commanded and specified its method?

Allāh commanded us to adorn the Qurʾān by beautifying our voices.

Where, then, did you get the legislation to use instruments?

Or did it not occur to you that these effects carry a legal ruling?

Be careful: you have introduced them into an act of worship.

text.text: Whoever Desires the Aid of Allâh ﷻ… Let Him Aid His Creation

text:
✍ Ibnul-Qayyim رحمه الله said:

“Shaykh ul-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah would search a lot to find people to help them with their needs. This was because he knew that every time he helped someone, then Allâh ﷻ would aid him.”
📖 Rawḍat al-Muḥibbīn (1/168)

This is a powerful secret of tawfīq.

Many of us sit waiting for relief…
Waiting for duʿā’ to be answered…
Waiting for doors to open…
Yet the key may be in serving someone else.

Allâh ﷻ says:

إِن تَنصُرُوا اللَّهَ يَنصُرْكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ

“If you help (the cause of) Allâh, He will help you and make your feet firm.”
~ (Muḥammad 47:7)

Part of helping the cause of Allâh ﷻ is helping His servants — easing their burdens, concealing their faults, feeding their hunger, teaching their ignorance, and comforting their grief.

💫 The Messenger of Allâh (ﷺ) said:
“Allâh is in the aid of His servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.”

When you rush to solve someone’s problem, Allâh ﷻ arranges solutions for yours.

When you wipe someone’s tears, Allâh ﷻ lifts distress from your heart.

When you give sincerely, Allâh ﷻ gives you from ways you never expected.

If you want Allâh ﷻ's support — become a means of support.

If you want doors opened — open doors for others.

May Allâh ﷻ make us keys to goodness and locks against evil.

messages.text:
{ لِیُنفِقۡ ذُو سَعَةࣲ مِّن سَعَتِهِۦۖ وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَیۡهِ رِزۡقُهُۥ فَلۡیُنفِقۡ مِمَّاۤ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُۚ لَا یُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا مَاۤ ءَاتَىٰهَاۚ سَیَجۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ عُسۡرࣲ یُسۡرࣰا }
[سُورَةُ الطَّلَاقِ: ٧]

"Let the rich man spend according to his means; and the man whose resources are restricted, let him spend according to what Allāh has given him. Allāh puts no burden on any person beyond what He has given him. Allāh will grant after hardship, ease".

Tr. Muhsin Khan and Taqi-ud-Din al-Hilali

messages.text:
Spend whatever Allāh has blessed you with.

Money, time, knowledge, an listening ear, a comforting word, a smile, guidance.

Whatever could bring joy and relief to your believing brothers/sisters. Anything that eases their hardships.

The secret is probably that, easing someone's affairs makes them more willing and able to do good themselves, and you were a cause of that.

Causing more good is a cause to more good. More good means more ease to all of us.

See how it all works together.

A hive of bees!

A distressed bee cannot help making honey...

text:
I see you.

Scrolling quietly.
Saving posts.
Wondering if you are doing enough.

You see beautifully organized shelves.
Perfectly printed planners.
Children reciting flawlessly on camera.

And then you look at your home…

The half-finished lesson.
The toddler interrupting.
The laundry waiting.
Your own exhaustion.

And you think,
“Maybe I’m behind.”

But let me tell you something gently:

A Qur’ānic home does not grow loudly.

It grows slowly.
It grows quietly.
It grows in repetition.
It grows in unseen moments.

It grows when you repeat an āyah for the tenth time.
When you correct a character flaw patiently.
When you answer a question about Allaah with sincerity.
When you choose consistency over perfection.

Roots do not grow on the surface.
They grow deep in the dark where no one applauds.

And depth always takes longer than display.

If your days feel simple…
If your progress feels small…
If no one is clapping…

That does not mean you are behind.

It means you are building something that lasts.

You are not raising content.
You are raising believers.

You are not building aesthetics.
You are building foundations.

You are building roots, not reels. 🌿

And roots, my dear parent,
are what hold a tree steady when storms come.

Keep going.

بارك الله فيك

بَكى صاحِبي لَمّا رَأى الدَربَ دونَنا

messages.text:
It's good to have phases where your illness, for those with chronic ones, intensifies until it puts you to bed, and interrupts your work.

You get time to realize you're weak, have no control, no might, no power, except what Allāh grants you.

You also get time to learn how to slow down, and pay attention to the things you were oblivious of while you were in your momentum.

If you were stupid enough to push your body until it had to cripple you into bed, then you'll also get time to repent from that, as your body has a right over you. Suffering is not virtue. It's actually a sin if you don't take the permissions Allāh legislated for us.

And of course, if you seek reward for your illness, you're being auto-cleaned, ان شاء الله.
Does it help if you think about the intensity of pain and discomfort mirrored by reward? It should.

Take a few moments to remember that you can eat and sleep and walk just fine, and make duʿāʾ for your ill brothers and sisters, here and there, whenever you remember them, or see someone ill.

نسأل الله أن يخفف عن إخوتنا وأخواتنا.

text:
Be patient. Allāh has placed you exactly where you are.  

Do not rush, do not resent what unfolds. Every moment moves according to His decree. Your task is to act; the outcome belongs to Him.  

Work with the tools you have. Move within the conditions He has given. Every limitation, every challenge, a part of the path He prepared for you.  

Do not chase what is not ready yet. Do not cling to what has passed. Step faithfully, adjust wisely, and trust that each moment carries its purpose.  

Patience is not waiting for life to change.  
Patience is moving rightly while it does not.

What is yours will be yours; it is just not ready yet.

text:
A beautiful, offline-first Arabic vocabulary app. Full tashkeel, spaced repetition, and two practice modes. Built for serious learners.

Learning Arabic is an act of worship. Whether you want to understand the Qurʾān more deeply, follow a khuṭbah, or simply make duʿāʾ without translating in your head — it starts with words.

Vocabulary Harvest is a clean, focused Arabic vocabulary app built for English-speaking learners who mean it.

🌱 800+ Arabic words across 55 lessons — from greetings and numbers to health, travel, and beyond
📖 Full tashkeel (vowel marks) on every word — so you learn correct pronunciation from the start
🧠 Spaced repetition (SM-2) — the app remembers which words you struggle with and brings them back at the right time
🌾 Two practice modes — Recall, and Assemble
🔊 Clear audio pronunciation for every word: requires internet connection · falls back to device TTS offline
📴 Fully offline after first load — no internet needed
✦ Custom categories — add your own words
💾 Export and import your progress — never lose your data

One-time purchase. No subscription. Free updates.

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

هذا التطبيق يقدّم كتابًا تعليميًا للأطفال والمبتدئين في عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة، بعنوان «منتقى كنز الأطفال»، من إعداد الأستاذ فيصل بن مسفر الوادعي.

* يضمّ التطبيق ٣٠٨ سؤالًا وجوابًا موزّعة على ١٦ بابًا، مع مقطع صوتي لكل سؤال.
* يمكن تصفّح الأسئلة بابًا بابًا، أو البحث بالكلمة في ثوانٍ، وحفظ الأسئلة المفضّلة للرجوع إليها لاحقًا.
* يحتوي التطبيق على قسم اختبار بأربعة أنماط مختلفة: الاختيار، وترتيب الجواب، وإكمال الكلمة الناقصة، والتعرّف على الجواب بالاستماع.
* كما يتتبع التطبيق نقاط الضعف تلقائيًا ويقترح مراجعتها.
* التطبيق يعمل بدون إنترنت بعد أول زيارة — إذ يمكن تثبيته على شاشة الهاتف كتطبيق عادي من خلال زر «إضافة إلى الشاشة الرئيسية»، ويعمل بشكل كامل حتى في غياب الاتصال بالشبكة.
  

مبادرة فردية لنشر هذا الكتاب القيّم بطريقة منظّمة وسهلة، بدون إعلانات أو تتبّع للمستخدمين، ومجانية تمامًا.

Step 0: Rely upon Allah.
Step 1: Calm down. Most bad decisions come from panic.
Step 2: Look at the skills Allāh gave you.
Step 3: Find a real problem that's within the radar of those skills. Solve that.
Step 4: Calm down again. Don't chase every new idea.
Step 5: Be patient.
Step 6: Calm down again. Progress is usually slower than your emotions want.
Step 7: Don't hook yourself to people. Collaboration can help, but dependency slows you down.
Step 8: Ask Allāh for tawfīq.

That’s basically it. No marketing fluff. No fear amplification. No manufactured scarcity.

Life is simple, if you let it be.

All that noise humans make, and in the end, it's just about food, drink, housing, bla bla bla.

As long as you can currently learn and worship Allāh... who's better than you huh?

Don't mind the slow progress and the loud noises. Everyone seems to move, but then...for what...ultimately?

May Allāh forgive us and you.

messages.text:
Most people try to learn languages backwards.

They begin with grammar rules, charts, verb tables, and technical explanations. They analyze the language before they even have enough words to think with. It feels serious, but it starves the brain of what it actually needs.

Words.

Your brain cannot build meaning from rules alone. Grammar is structure, but vocabulary is substance. Grammar arranges thoughts — vocabulary creates them.

This quote captures it perfectly:

"Without grammar, little can be conveyed. Without vocabulary, nothing can be conveyed".

Think about how children learn language. A toddler doesn't memorize verb paradigms or grammatical cases. A toddler absorbs words. Thousands of them. Slowly, naturally, instinctively.

Once the brain has enough words, patterns begin to emerge on their own.

This is not guesswork. It is how human language acquisition works.

Vocabulary Harvest is built around that simple truth.

Instead of drowning you in rules, it feeds your mind what it actually needs: raw linguistic material. Words with full tashkīl so you see the language correctly from the beginning. Spaced repetition so the brain meets each word again exactly when it is about to forget it. Practice modes that force recall so the words stop being symbols and start becoming instinct.

Over time something remarkable happens.

The language stops feeling like a puzzle you must solve. It begins to feel like a landscape you can move through.

You start recognizing words in khuṭbahs. In books. In Qurʾān recitation. The shapes become familiar. Meanings appear instantly instead of after translation.

This is the moment when Arabic stops being studied and starts being embodied.

Vocabulary Harvest is not trying to impress you with complexity.

It is doing something much more powerful.

It gives your mind the raw material it needs to build the language itself.

It relieves your mind of the dead weight you've been carrying.

It frees your brain through simplicity and minimalism.

text.text:
Why Al-Albaany Spoke to People Like They Were His Peers

Anyone who listens to al-Albaany's recorded discussions notices that he didn't talk down to people. Whether the person in front of him was a beginner or a student of knowledge, he spoke to them with a calm confidence, inviting them into the reasoning process rather than placing them at the bottom of a ladder.


He didn't do this because he saw no difference between levels of knowledge. He did it because he respected a person's ability to think.

His method was simple: present the evidence clearly, ask for proof in return, and move forward step by step. The conversation felt like two people cooperating to find the truth, not a teacher crushing a student under his library.


That style is refreshing today, especially when so many discussions feel scripted or overly formal.

Al-Albaany's approach had a certain sharpness, but it wasn't harshness. It was confidence in the strength of proof. The science carried the authority; he didn't need to.


This is why his tapes still feel alive. They're not lectures to passive listeners. They're dialogues that pull you in and insist you think and reason!

https://en-armalqaddaaree.blogspot.com/2025/12/why-al-albaany-spoke-to-people-like.html

text:
Questioner: How does a Muslim know that he has encountered Laylat al-Qadr while dilgently seeking it during the nights that are narrated from the Prophet ﷺ?

Al-ʾImām al-ʾAlbānī -may Allāh have mercy on him-: That is a sentimental matter felt by everyone whom Allāh—Blessed and Exalted is He—has favored to witness Laylat al-Qadr. This is because on this night the person turns to worshiping Allāh—Mighty and Majestic is He—to His remembrance, and to prayer. Allāh—Mighty and Majestic—then reveals to some of His servants a feeling that not even the righteous experience at other times, this feeling is what can be relied upon.

ʿĀʾishah -may Allāh be pleased with her- conveyed to the Messenger ﷺ a question that indicates whether a person can sense witnessing Laylat al-Qadr.

text.text: She asked the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allāh, if I know which night is Laylat al-Qadr, what should I say during it?" He said: «Say: O Allāh, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me.»

text:
In this ḥadīth, there are two benefits:

1- A Muslim can have a personal, subjective feeling of encountering Laylat al-Qadr. 
2- If he feels that, the best supplication to make is this one: "O Allāh, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me."

On this occasion, it is mentioned this book of ours, "At-Targhīb," in some lessons, that the best thing a person can ask his Lord—Blessed and Exalted is He—is for pardon and well-being (ʿāfiyah) in this world and the Hereafter.

Yes, there are some signs and physical indicators of Laylat al-Qadr, but not everyone who witnesses and knows Laylat al-Qadr can see these. That is because some of these signs relate to the general external atmosphere. For example, the night might be neither hot nor cold, but rather temperate. However, a person might be in an environment where he cannot perceive the natural climate of the area.

There is also a sign, but it appears after Laylat al-Qadr in the morning of that night at sunrise. The Prophet ﷺ informed us that the sun rises on the morning of Laylat al-Qadr appearing like a moon, without rays. That is how the sun rises on the morning of Laylat al-Qadr, and this has been observed by some righteous people who cared about seeing and noticing it on many nights of Laylat al-Qadr.

What's important regarding the devoted worshipper is not to cling to such physical phenomena, because these phenomena are general, meaning they pertain to the nature of the climate. Not everyone who lives in that climate shares in witnessing Laylat al-Qadr, meaning: in having that spiritual clarity at one of the moments during that blessed night, such that Allāh—Mighty and Majestic—bestows upon them His mercy and grace, inspiring one and causing him to supplicate with what has preceded along with other supplications.

Verily physical signs are signs, but they do not indicate that everyone who witnesses or experiences them has attained Laylat al-Qadr—and this is the reality. However, the aspect that should be focused on is the spiritual clarity within oneself and the feeling of witnessing Laylat al-Qadr, and turning to Allāh with prescribed supplications.

This is the aspect we should focus on and be concerned with, hoping that Allāh—Mighty and Majestic—may bestow it upon us by His grace.

اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ، فَاعْفُ عَنِّي.

Allāhumma Innaka ʿAfuwwun tuḥibbu al-ʿafwa, faʿfu ʿannī.

.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ،
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي،
اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي،
اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ وَمِنْ خَلْفِي وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي وَمِنْ فَوْقِي،
وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي.

Allāhumma innī asʾaluka al-ʿāfiyata fī ad-dunyā wa al-ākhirah.
Allāhumma innī asʾaluka al-ʿafwa wa al-ʿāfiyata fī dīnī wa-dunyāya wa-ahlī wa-mālī.
Allāhumma stur ʿawrātī wa āmin rawʿātī.
Allāhumma ḥfaẓnī min bayni yadayya wa-min khalfī wa-ʿan yamīnī wa-ʿan shimālī wa-min fawqī,
wa-aʿūthu bi-ʿAẓamatika an ughtāla min taḥtī.

text.text: The Passing Wind And The Blind

text:
Even a passing wind has aim,
it moves with force, direction, and claim.

Not every wind becomes a storm —
yet bends the branch and shifts the form.

The dunes are carved by grains of sand,
not by the thunder's heavy hand.

The stone is worn by what persists,
not sudden strikes from angry fists.

The seed is carried and fields are grown,
by what you barely felt or known.

The blind eye names it nothing still —
the valley fills against its will.

You know...

The blind eye names it nothing still —
the valley fills against its will.

You know...

messages.text:
Gentleness ~ الرِّفق

Gentleness is not weakness, nor is it the abandonment of truth. Rather, it is the discipline of the heart when it holds truth. It is strength guided by mercy.
الرِّفقُ ليس ضعفًا، ولا هو تخلٍّ عن الحق. بل هو انضباطُ القلب حين يحمل الحقَّ. إنه القوةُ التي تسوسها الرحمة.

The world is filled with people who carry unseen wounds.
العالمُ مليءٌ بأناسٍ يحملون جراحًا لا تُرى.

Some walk with grief buried deep within them.
منهم من يمشي وفي أعماقه حزنٌ دفين.

Some struggle with loneliness that no one around them notices.
 ومنهم من يعاني وحدةً لا يلحظها من حوله.

Others carry the weight of their own mistakes and shortcomings.
وآخرون يثقل كاهلَهم وِزرُ أخطائهم وتقصيرهم.

From the outside they may appear composed, even strong, yet within them there is turmoil greater than you can fathom.
 قد يبدون من الخارج هادئين، بل أقوياء، غير أن في داخلهم من الاضطراب ما يفوق ما تتصور.

A harsh word may seem small to the one who utters it, yet to the one already burdened it can feel like the final stone placed upon a heavy load.
وقد تبدو الكلمةُ القاسية صغيرةً في نظر قائلها، لكنها على من هو مثقلٌ بالأعباء كالحجرة الأخيرة التي تُوضَع فوق حِمل ثقيل.

Harshness rarely reforms hearts. More often it causes hearts to retreat, to close themselves, and to protect what little peace remains within them.
والقسوةُ نادرًا ما تُصلح القلوب، بل كثيرًا ما تجعلها تنكمش وتنغلق، تحمي ما تبقّى فيها من سكينة.

This is why gentleness has always been the path that reaches people.
لهذا كان الرِّفقُ دائمًا هو الطريق الذي يصل إلى الناس.

The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said:
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ»
"Indeed, Allāh is Gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters."
— [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī | صحيح البخاري]

Gentleness is not merely a tone of voice. It is a way of seeing people.
والرِّفقُ ليس مجرد نبرة صوت. إنه طريقةٌ في رؤية الناس.

It is the ability to recognise that every person you encounter is fighting battles you cannot see. It is to understand that guidance grows in an atmosphere of mercy, not intimidation.
إنه القدرة على إدراك أن كل شخص تلقاه يخوض معاركَ لا تراها. وأن الهداية تنمو في أجواء الرحمة لا في أجواء الترهيب.

History shows that hearts are not conquered by force.
والتاريخ يشهد أن القلوب لا تُفتح بالقوة،

They are conquered by patience and compassion.
بل تُفتح بالصبر والحنان.

A person who feels understood becomes open to change.
فمن يشعر بأنه مفهومٌ تنفتح نفسه للتغيير،

A person who feels attacked becomes defensive, even if the truth is clear before them.
 ومن يشعر بأنه مهاجَمٌ يتحصَّن ويدافع، حتى وإن كان الحقُّ جليًّا أمامه.

For this reason Allāh commanded gentleness even in the face of arrogance and tyranny.
لهذا أمر اللهُ بالرِّفق حتى في مواجهة الكبر والطغيان.

When Mūsā and Hārūn عليهما السلام were sent to the most tyrannical ruler of their time, they were instructed:
حين أُرسل موسى وهارون عليهما السلام إلى أشد الحكام طغيانا في زمانهما، أُمِرا:

{ فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا }
"Speak to him with gentle speech."
— [Ṭāhā: 44 | طه: ٤٤]

If gentleness was commanded even when addressing Pharaoh — a man who claimed lordship over people, oppressed an entire nation, and ordered the slaughter of innocent children — then how much more should it exist between ordinary people?
فإن كان الرِّفقُ مأمورًا به في مخاطبة فرعون — الذي ادّعى الربوبية، وقهر أمةً بأسرها، وأمر بذبح الأطفال الأبرياء — فكم يكون أولى أن يسود بين عامة الناس؟

Too often we see someone who is merely mistaken or misguided and instinctively respond with harshness, imagining it to be strength.
وكثيرًا ما نرى من هو مخطئٌ أو ضال عن الحق، فنبادر إلى القسوة ظنًّا أنها قوة.

In reality, it is often weakness and a lack of understanding. True firmness upon the truth does not abandon gentleness; it is disciplined enough to carry the truth without allowing arrogance, anger, or impatience to corrupt the way it is delivered.
وفي الحقيقة، هي في الغالب ضعفٌ وقصورٌ في الفهم. فالثبات الحقيقي على الحق لا يتخلى عن الرِّفق، بل له من الانضباط بحيث يحمل الحقَّ دون أن يُفسد أسلوبَ إيصاله تكبُّرٌ أو غضبٌ أو عجلة.

text:
The hearts of people are delicate things. When gentleness disappears, relationships become rigid, advice becomes unbearable, and truth itself begins to feel heavy upon those who hear it.
قلوبُ الناس رقيقة. فإذا ما غاب الرِّفق، تجمّدت العلاقات، وصارت النصيحة لا تُطاق، وبدا الحقُّ ثقيلًا على سامعيه.

But when gentleness is present, even difficult words can be received withي openness.
أما حين يحضر الرِّفق فحتى الكلماتُ الصعبة تُتلقَّى بانفتاح.

The one who carries gentleness within them becomes a source of relief for others. Their presence brings calm rather than tension. Their speech heals rather than wounds. Their character reminds people that mercy still exists in a world that often feels severe.
ومن حمل الرِّفقَ في نفسه صار مصدرَ راحة للآخرين. حضورُه يجلب السكينة لا التوتر، وكلامُه يشفي لا يجرح، وخُلُقُه يُذكّر الناس بأن الرحمة لا تزال موجودةً في عالمٍ كثيرًا ما يبدو قاسيًا.

And this is perhaps one of the greatest forms of service to humanity: to be someone through whom others feel safe enough to soften their hearts.
وهذا ربما من أعظم صور الخدمة للإنسانية: أن تكون شخصًا يشعر عنده الآخرون بالأمان الكافي ليُليّنوا قلوبهم.

So remain firm upon truth, but clothe that firmness with gentleness. For harshness may silence people, but gentleness reaches their hearts. And hearts, once reached with gentleness, are capable of transformation that force could never achieve.
فاثبت على الحق، لكن البَس هذا الثباتَ بالرِّفق. فالقسوةُ قد تُسكت الناس، لكن الرِّفق يصل إلى قلوبهم. والقلوب إذا بلغها الرِّفقُ قدرت على تحوُّلٍ لا تستطيعه القوة أبدًا.

Life is brief, and people are weary. What they need most is not more severity, but more mercy.
الحياةُ قصيرة، والناس متعبون. وما يحتاجونه أكثر من أي شيء ليس مزيدًا من الشدة، بل مزيدًا من الرحمة.

أبو رفق
٢٣ رمضان ١٤٤٧ هـ

Translated to Arabic by:
Abu Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mihūb al-Qaddārī

messages.text:
I care little for structured learning. I have never been drawn to systems that force a person through a fixed path simply because that path was designed beforehand.

What I know, I learned in a different way.
I follow questions.

When something in my life creates friction, a problem, a doubt, a gap in my understanding: my curiosity triggers.

I begin searching until all pieces are flat and separate on the ground. I read, compare, test, and think until the picture settles.

Then I move on.

Knowledge, for me, accumulates as a side-effect of trying to understand what confronts me in life.

This way of learning is uneven. Some areas become deep and detailed because interest pulled me there. Other areas remain untouched because nothing ever pushed me to look into them.

I accept that.

Academic and similar systems attempt to remove such unevenness. They impose structure, pacing, and predetermined routes so that everyone moves through the same terrain.

But that's rigid. Not everyone learns that way.

Some of us learn by pursuit. By hunger. By the quiet urge to uncover what we do not yet understand.

That is the path I took, and the one I intend to keep.

Language 2: I learned English through content consumption, and communicating with English speakers.

Language 3: I learned French through...lessons and rules. My weakest language in the set. To be fair, I don't even like French, so that's a reason. Baguette.

Language 4: I wonder what personality I could unlock with Russian. What people I could meet. How would I express myself in Russian? It's an elegant language, something I've been fascinated by for a while. It sounds mesmerizing, to say the least. I'm not a Russian spy, I promise.

messages.text:
الحمد لله حمداً كثيراً طيباً مباركاً فيه، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، أما بعد:
In the Name of Allāh, the Merciful, the All-Merciful. All praise is due to Allāh, a praise that is plentiful, pure, and blessed. I bear witness that there is no god except Allāh alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His slave and Messenger.
To proceed:
فإن الاهتمام بـ:
• تعليم الصغار.
• وتفقيههم في دين الله.
مطلبٌ عظيمٌ؛ حثّ عليه كتاب ربنا، وسنة نبينا محمد ﷺ.
Focusing on:
    • Teaching the young.
    • Granting them understanding of the religion of Allāh.
This is a great objective encouraged by the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of our Prophet Muḥammad ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam.
فقد صح عند الترمذي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال له: « يا غلام إني أعلمك كلمات ...... » الحديث.
It was authentically reported by at-Tirmithi, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with them), that the Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said to him: "O young man, I shall teach you some words..." (the ḥadīth).
وصح عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: «علموا صبيانكم الصلاة في سبع سنين ...... » الحديث. 
And it was authentically reported from ʿAbdullāh bnu ʿAmr (may Allāh be pleased with them) that the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said: "Teach your children prayer at seven years..." (the ḥadīth).
وإن التعليم على طريقة السؤال والجواب لهي:
• طريقةٌ نبويةٌ مفيدةٌ، 
Teaching through the question-and-answer method is:
    • A beneficial Prophetic method.
وقد قال النبي ﷺ لمعاذ رضي الله عنه: «أتدري ما حق الله على العباد؟ وما حق العباد على الله؟» 
The Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said to Muʿāth (may Allāh be pleased with him): "Do you know what is the right of Allāh over His slaves? And what is the right of the slaves over Allāh?"
وقال ﷺ في حديث آخر: «إن من الشجر شجرة مثلها مثل المسلم لا يسقط ورقها أخبروني ما هي».
In another Hadith, he, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said: "Indeed, among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is that of a Muslim; its leaves do not fall. Tell me, which one is it?"
وهذه الطريقة:
• أقرب إلى الفهم والتفهيم.
• وأوضح في التعلم والتعليم.
This method:
    • Is closer to [achieving] understanding and comprehension.
    • Is clearer for learning and teaching.
ومن هنا؛ فهذه مجموعة أسئلة يزيد عددها على الألف سؤال، كتبتها بطريقة مختصرة: 
Hence, this is a collection of questions numbering more than a thousand, which I have written in a concise manner.
احتوت على أهم المهمات من أمور الدين، وأصول الإيمان، ومبادئ الفقه، والآداب، والمعاملات، والسيرة، وغيرها. تدعوا الحاجة والضرورة إلى معرفتها. 
It contains the most important matters of religion: the foundations of faith (īmān), principles of jurisprudence (Fiqh), etiquette (Adab), transactions (Muʿāmalāt), biography (Sīrah), and others—matters for which there is a pressing need and necessity to know.
خصصتها للصغار ولا يستغني عنها الكبار.
I have designated it for the young, though adults cannot do without it either.
وقد تحريت جهدي أن تكون جميع الأسئلة مبنيةً على أدلة صحيحة من الكتاب والسنة. 
I have strived to ensure all questions are based on authentic evidence from the Book and the Sunnah.
لكني لم أذكر الأدلة:
However, I did not mention the evidence [here]:
أولاً: لطلب الاختصار. ثانياً: لأن هذا سيكون -إن شاء الله- في كتاب آخر؛ يكون بمثابة الشرح والتوسع في هذه الأسئلة. ثالثاً: يكون هذا القدر من الجواب هو المطلوب من الصغير أن يحفظه، ويقوم المدرس بشرح الجواب، وذكر الدليل على ذلك.

    2.  Because this will be—if Allāh wills—in another book that will serve as an explanation and expansion of these questions.
    3.  So that this amount of the answer is what the child is required to memorize, while the teacher explains the answer and mentions the evidence for it.

الحمد لله حمداً كثيراً طيباً مباركاً فيه، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، أما بعد:
In the Name of Allāh, the Merciful, the All-Merciful. All praise is due to Allāh, a praise that is plentiful, pure, and blessed. I bear witness that there is no god except Allāh alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His slave and Messenger.
To proceed:
فإن الاهتمام بـ:
• تعليم الصغار.
• وتفقيههم في دين الله.
مطلبٌ عظيمٌ؛ حثّ عليه كتاب ربنا، وسنة نبينا محمد ﷺ.
Focusing on:
    • Teaching the young.
    • Granting them understanding of the religion of Allāh.
This is a great objective encouraged by the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of our Prophet Muḥammad ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam.
فقد صح عند الترمذي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال له: « يا غلام إني أعلمك كلمات ...... » الحديث.
It was authentically reported by at-Tirmithi, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with them), that the Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said to him: "O young man, I shall teach you some words..." (the ḥadīth).
وصح عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: «علموا صبيانكم الصلاة في سبع سنين ...... » الحديث. 
And it was authentically reported from ʿAbdullāh bnu ʿAmr (may Allāh be pleased with them) that the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said: "Teach your children prayer at seven years..." (the ḥadīth).
وإن التعليم على طريقة السؤال والجواب لهي:
• طريقةٌ نبويةٌ مفيدةٌ، 
Teaching through the question-and-answer method is:
    • A beneficial Prophetic method.
وقد قال النبي ﷺ لمعاذ رضي الله عنه: «أتدري ما حق الله على العباد؟ وما حق العباد على الله؟» 
The Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said to Muʿāth (may Allāh be pleased with him): "Do you know what is the right of Allāh over His slaves? And what is the right of the slaves over Allāh?"
وقال ﷺ في حديث آخر: «إن من الشجر شجرة مثلها مثل المسلم لا يسقط ورقها أخبروني ما هي».
In another Hadith, he, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said: "Indeed, among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is that of a Muslim; its leaves do not fall. Tell me, which one is it?"
وهذه الطريقة:
• أقرب إلى الفهم والتفهيم.
• وأوضح في التعلم والتعليم.
This method:
    • Is closer to [achieving] understanding and comprehension.
    • Is clearer for learning and teaching.

The Muntaqā edition (308 questions) includes a recorded audio recitation for every single question and answer.

---

- Questions are organized into chapters and presented as interactive flip cards — tap a card to reveal the answer with a smooth 3D animation.  
- The full list loads progressively so even the largest book feels instant.  
- A search bar lets you find any question or answer in seconds, with fuzzy Arabic matching that handles spelling variations and strips diacritics automatically.  
- Search results highlight the matched text and auto-flip cards to the answer face when the match is found there.  
- You can filter by chapter at any time, both in the main view and inside search.

---

- Any card can be starred and saved to a personal favorites list, which persists across sessions.  
- The favorites view gives you quick access to the questions you want to revisit most.

---

The quiz section lets you test yourself on any chapter or the full book, with 5, 10, or 20 questions at a time. Four distinct modes keep practice engaging:

1.

— read the question and pick the correct answer from four options.  
2.

— the answer is split into shuffled word tiles; tap them in the right order to reconstruct it. Placed tiles can be tapped again to return them to the pool.  
3.

— the answer is shown with its most meaningful word hidden; choose the correct word from four options.  
4.

— the audio recording plays and you identify the correct answer from four choices, training your ear alongside your memory.  

- The app tracks your performance automatically.  
- Any question you get wrong more often than right gets flagged as a weak spot, and a dedicated *Weak Spots* section appears in the chapter selector so you can drill exactly what needs work.

---

- Every question in the Muntaqā edition has a native-quality audio recording.  
- Audio plays on both the front and back of flip cards, synced across both faces.  
- Audio also plays during the Listen quiz mode.  
- The app caches all 308 audio files in the background after the first visit, so they play offline without any delay.

text:
I'd really love if we stopped decorating people with labels, especially the living. 
No matter how "big" someone seems.

Just call them

and move on. 

Saves you from exaggeration and from saying things that aren't true.

Some don't even deserve the title

, yet it's been used so much it barely means anything now.

Dr. Fayṣal al-Wādiʿī still treats the word with weight and refuses to adopt it. More people like that would be nice. May Allāh bless him.

When al-Albānī lowered himself and al-Wādiʿī said, "we're basically nothing at this point", what does that say about the rest of us?

Yes, that was humility. But also honesty. They knew the level of the scholars before them and knew they were nowhere near them.

Strange thing: the lower the level gets, the bigger the labels become.

عجيب.
